questions.explanation: Ciliated protozoans like Paramoecium have a gullet opening to the cell surface for feeding.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Malaria is caused by:
questions.explanation: Plasmodium, a sporozoan, is the malarial parasite with a staggering effect on human population.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Kingdom Fungi is characterised by organisms that are:
questions.explanation: Fungi form a unique kingdom of heterotrophic organisms with great morphological diversity.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Yeast is used in:
questions.explanation: Unicellular yeast (Saccharomyces) is used in bread and beer production.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Puccinia causes:
questions.explanation: Puccinia is an important rust fungus causing wheat rust.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Penicillium is notable as a source of:
questions.explanation: Penicillium is an example of fungi that produce antibiotics.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Fungi prefer to grow in:
questions.explanation: Fungi are cosmopolitan but prefer warm, humid environments—hence refrigeration slows spoilage.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The network of fungal hyphae is called:
questions.explanation: Fungal bodies are filamentous; hyphae collectively form the mycelium.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Hyphae that are continuous multinucleate tubes without septa are:
questions.explanation: Coenocytic hyphae are continuous tubes with multinucleated cytoplasm and no cross walls.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Fungal cell walls are composed of:
questions.explanation: Fungal cell walls contain chitin and polysaccharides.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Fungal symbiotic associations include:
questions.option_d: Lichens with algae and mycorrhiza with plant roots
questions.explanation: Fungi form lichens with algae and mycorrhiza with roots of higher plants.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Fusion of protoplasms between two gametes in fungi is termed:
questions.explanation: Plasmogamy is fusion of protoplasms between two gametes in the fungal sexual cycle.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Fusion of two nuclei in fungi is called:
questions.explanation: Karyogamy is nuclear fusion following plasmogamy in fungal reproduction.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: A dikaryon in fungi refers to:
questions.option_b: A cell with two nuclei per cell (n + n)
questions.option_c: A cell with one haploid nucleus
questions.explanation: In ascomycetes and basidiomycetes, a dikaryotic (n + n) stage with two nuclei per cell occurs before karyogamy.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Phycomycetes are commonly found:
questions.option_c: In aquatic habitats and on decaying wood in moist places
questions.explanation: Phycomycetes inhabit aquatic environments, moist decaying wood or act as obligate plant parasites.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Mycelium of phycomycetes is:
questions.explanation: Phycomycetes have aseptate coenocytic mycelium.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Bread mould belongs to genus:
questions.explanation: Rhizopus is the bread mould; Mucor and Albugo (mustard parasite) are also phycomycetes.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Sac-fungi belong to class:
questions.explanation: Ascomycetes are commonly called sac-fungi; examples include Penicillium and yeast (Saccharomyces).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Sexual spores of ascomycetes produced inside sac-like asci are:
questions.explanation: Ascospores are produced endogenously within sac-like asci in ascomycetes.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Neurospora is extensively used in:
questions.explanation: Neurospora is an ascomycete used extensively in biochemical and genetic research.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Mushrooms belong to class:
questions.explanation: Mushrooms, bracket fungi and puffballs are common basidiomycete forms.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Basidiospores in basidiomycetes are produced:
questions.option_c: Exogenously on the basidium after karyogamy and meiosis
questions.explanation: Karyogamy and meiosis occur in the basidium, yielding four exogenous basidiospores.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Ustilago is a:
questions.explanation: Ustilago causes smut; Puccinia causes rust; Agaricus is the common mushroom.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Deuteromycetes are called imperfect fungi because:
questions.option_c: Only their asexual or vegetative phases are known
questions.explanation: Deuteromycetes are imperfect fungi whose sexual stages were unknown or later placed in other classes.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which of the following is a deuteromycete?
questions.explanation: Alternaria, Colletotrichum and Trichoderma are examples of deuteromycetes.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Kingdom Plantae includes:
questions.explanation: Plantae comprises eukaryotic chlorophyll-containing organisms commonly called plants.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Cuscuta is an example of:
questions.explanation: Cuscuta is a parasitic plant; Bladderwort and Venus fly trap are insectivorous plants.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which group is included in Kingdom Plantae?
questions.explanation: Plantae includes algae, bryophytes, pteridophytes, gymnosperms and angiosperms.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Alternation of generations in plants refers to alternation between:
questions.option_d: Diploid sporophytic and haploid gametophytic phases
questions.explanation: Plant life cycles alternate between diploid sporophytic and haploid gametophytic generations.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Kingdom Animalia is characterised by:
questions.option_a: Heterotrophic multicellular eukaryotes lacking cell walls
questions.explanation: Animalia includes heterotrophic, multicellular eukaryotes whose cells lack cell walls.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Food reserves in animals are stored as:
questions.explanation: Animals store food reserves as glycogen or fat.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The typical mode of nutrition in Kingdom Animalia is:
questions.explanation: Animals are holozoic—they ingest and internally digest food.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which acellular entities are NOT included in Whittaker's five kingdom classification?
questions.explanation: Whittaker's system does not include viruses, viroids, prions or lichens.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Outside the host cell, viruses exist as:
questions.explanation: Viruses are non-cellular and form inert crystals outside their specific host cells.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Who demonstrated in 1892 that mosaic disease of tobacco is caused by microbes smaller than bacteria?
questions.explanation: Dmitri Ivanowsky (1892) showed tobacco mosaic is caused by filter-passing microbes smaller than bacteria.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The term 'virus' and 'Contagium vivum fluidum' were coined by:
questions.explanation: Beijerinck (1898) named the pathogen 'virus' and termed the infectious fluid Contagium vivum fluidum.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Who showed in 1935 that viruses could be crystallised?
questions.explanation: W.M. Stanley (1935) crystallised viruses, showing crystals consist largely of proteins.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Regarding viral genetic material:
questions.option_a: All viruses contain both RNA and DNA
questions.option_b: No virus contains both RNA and DNA
questions.option_c: Only DNA is present in all viruses
questions.option_d: Only RNA is present in all viruses
questions.explanation: Viruses contain either RNA or DNA as genetic material, never both.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Plant viruses generally have:
questions.explanation: Plant-infecting viruses generally possess single-stranded RNA.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Bacteriophages usually contain:
questions.option_b: Only protein with no nucleic acid
questions.explanation: Bacteriophages (bacterial viruses) are usually double-stranded DNA viruses.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Protein subunits of the viral capsid are called:
questions.explanation: The capsid protecting viral nucleic acid is composed of capsomeres arranged helically or polyhedrally.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: AIDS in humans is caused by:
questions.explanation: AIDS is among viral diseases listed along with mumps, small pox, herpes and influenza.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Potato spindle tuber disease is caused by:
questions.option_a: A viroid discovered by T.O. Diener
questions.explanation: T.O. Diener (1971) discovered viroids causing potato spindle tuber disease.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Viroids differ from viruses because viroids:
questions.option_a: Are free RNA without a protein coat
questions.option_d: Are larger than viruses with capsids
questions.explanation: Viroids are free low molecular weight RNA lacking the protein coat present in viruses.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Mad cow disease (BSE) is caused by:
questions.explanation: BSE (mad cow disease) and CJD in humans are notable prion diseases involving abnormally folded proteins.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Lichens represent a symbiotic association between:
questions.explanation: Lichens are mutualistic associations between algae and fungi.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: In lichens, the algal partner is called:
questions.explanation: The algal (autotrophic) component is phycobiont; the fungal (heterotrophic) partner is mycobiont.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Lichens are useful as:
questions.option_a: Pollution indicators that avoid polluted areas
questions.explanation: Lichens are sensitive pollution indicators and do not grow in polluted areas.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: According to the chapter summary, biological classification was first proposed by Aristotle based on:
questions.explanation: The summary states Aristotle first proposed biological classification using simple morphological characters.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: How many classes of fungi are described in this chapter?
questions.explanation: The four fungal classes covered are Phycomycetes, Ascomycetes, Basidiomycetes and Deuteromycetes.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Sexual reproduction in fungi begins when:
questions.option_a: Two haploid hyphae of compatible mating types fuse
questions.explanation: Compatible haploid hyphae fuse to initiate the fungal sexual cycle.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Some marine amoeboid protozoans have:
questions.explanation: Marine amoeboid forms may bear silica shells on their surface.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: White spots on mustard leaves are caused by:
questions.explanation: Albugo is the parasitic fungus on mustard causing white spots; it is a phycomycete.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Viruses are excluded from Whittaker's five kingdom classification.
Reason (R): Viruses are acellular and show an inert crystalline form outside the host.
questions.option_a: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.option_b: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
questions.option_c: A is true but R is false
questions.option_d: A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: NCERT states viruses/viroids/prions/lichens are outside five kingdoms because they are not truly cellular living organisms in the conventional sense.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Ascomycetes and basidiomycetes show a dikaryophase (n+n).
Reason (R): In these fungi, karyogamy is delayed after plasmogamy.
questions.option_a: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.option_b: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
questions.option_c: A is true but R is false
questions.option_d: A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Dikaryon (two nuclei per cell) arises because nuclear fusion follows cytoplasmic fusion only after an intervening dikaryotic stage.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Mycoplasma are the smallest living cells known.
Reason (R): Absence of a rigid cell wall allows extreme reduction in cell size.
questions.option_a: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.option_b: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
questions.option_c: A is true but R is false
questions.option_d: A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: NCERT gives both facts independently; the text does not explicitly link small size to wall absence as cause-effect.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Nostoc and Anabaena are photosynthetic autotrophs.
Reason (R): They possess chlorophyll a like green plants.
questions.option_a: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.option_b: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
questions.option_c: A is true but R is false
questions.option_d: A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll a enables photosynthetic autotrophy in cyanobacteria; nitrogen fixation is a separate feature in heterocysts.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Trichoderma is grouped under Deuteromycetes.
Reason (R): Its perfect (sexual) stage was never observed when the group was defined.
questions.option_a: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.option_b: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
questions.option_c: A is true but R is false
questions.option_d: A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Deuteromycetes (imperfect fungi) are defined by known asexual stages only; Trichoderma is a textbook example.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Prions are smaller than typical bacteria.
Reason (R): Prions lack nucleic acid.
questions.option_a: Both A and R are true and R is NOT the correct explanation of A
questions.option_b: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.option_c: A is true but R is false
questions.option_d: A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Prions are virus-sized protein agents without genetic material; NCERT does not state size is because of no nucleic acid.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Paramoecium was earlier placed in Animalia.
Reason (R): Animalia includes only multicellular organisms.
questions.option_a: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.option_b: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
questions.option_c: A is true but R is false
questions.option_d: A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Paramoecium was earlier in Animalia, but Animalia in Whittaker's system includes heterotrophic eukaryotes that are multicellular—not exclusively so in older schemes; the stated reason is false.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Slime mould spores possess true walls and are air-dispersed.
Reason (R): Slime moulds are saprophytic protists.
questions.option_a: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.option_b: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
questions.option_c: A is true but R is false
questions.option_d: A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Spore wall formation and dispersal are independent of their saprophytic nutrition.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Such bacteria recycle nutrients like nitrogen and sulphur.
Reason (R): Energy released from oxidation of inorganics is used for ATP production.
questions.option_a: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.option_b: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
questions.option_c: A is true but R is false
questions.option_d: A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: ATP from chemosynthesis enables metabolism including nutrient cycling, but recycling is a broader ecological role not solely explained by ATP production.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Viroids were discovered by T.O. Diener in 1971.
Reason (R): Viroids cause potato spindle tuber disease.
questions.option_a: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.option_b: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
questions.option_c: A is true but R is false
questions.option_d: A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Diener discovered viroids while studying that disease, but discovery date is not explained by the disease itself.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Basidiospores are exogenously produced on basidia.
Reason (R): Meiosis occurs in the basidium.
questions.option_a: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.option_b: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
questions.option_c: A is true but R is false
questions.option_d: A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Meiosis in basidium produces haploid basidiospores that are borne externally, but exogenous production is a morphological fact not defined solely by meiosis location.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Chlamydomonas and Amoeba are both placed in Protista.
Reason (R): Earlier classification placed them in different kingdoms.
questions.option_a: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.option_b: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
questions.option_c: A is true but R is false
questions.option_d: A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: NCERT explicitly states Protista united organisms previously split between plant and animal kingdoms.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question:
Assertion (A): A virus is always a nucleoprotein.
Reason (R): Capsid proteins protect the single type of nucleic acid.
questions.option_a: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.option_b: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
questions.option_c: A is true but R is false
questions.option_d: A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Nucleoprotein nature comes from nucleic acid plus protein coat; protection by capsid does not define nucleoprotein status.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: In Table 2.1, which kingdom alone has a cell wall described as noncellulosic polysaccharide with amino acids?
questions.explanation: Monera alone has peptidoglycan-type noncellulosic walls; fungi have chitin, plants cellulose, protists variable.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: A student claims 'Protista never possess cell walls.' According to Table 2.1, the correct rebuttal is:
questions.option_a: Protista are prokaryotic and hence wall-less
questions.option_b: Cell wall is present in some protists
questions.option_d: Protista always lack walls like Animalia
questions.explanation: Table 2.1 explicitly states cell wall is 'Present in some' for Protista (e.g., diatoms, dinoflagellates) but absent in others (e.g., Amoeba).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which kingdom in Table 2.1 is the only one with 'Multicellular / loose tissue' as body organisation?
questions.explanation: Fungi alone show loose tissue-like multicellular mycelium; Protista and Monera are cellular, Plantae tissue/organ level.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Table 2.1 indicates that chemosynthetic autotrophy is a mode of nutrition in:
questions.option_a: Monera only among the five kingdoms listed
questions.explanation: Only Monera lists chemosynthetic autotrophy explicitly; Plantae is photosynthetic autotrophic only.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Holozoic nutrition is characteristic of which kingdom per Table 2.1?
questions.explanation: Table 2.1 lists holozoic nutrition under Animalia; fungi are saprophytic/parasitic heterotrophs.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: If an organism has a nuclear membrane and is unicellular, Table 2.1 would place it in:
questions.explanation: Unicellular + nuclear membrane = eukaryotic = Protista (among options); Monera lacks nuclear membrane.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: How many of the five Whittaker kingdoms in Table 2.1 are exclusively eukaryotic?
questions.explanation: Protista, Fungi, Plantae and Animalia are eukaryotic; only Monera is prokaryotic.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: An organism with tissue/organ organisation, holozoic nutrition and no cell wall fits Table 2.1 under:
questions.explanation: Animalia: tissue/organ/organ-system, heterotrophic holozoic, no cell wall.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Autotrophic nutrition is NOT listed for which two kingdoms in Table 2.1?
questions.explanation: Fungi and Animalia are exclusively heterotrophic per Table 2.1; Monera and Protista include autotrophic forms.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which pair correctly matches body organisation from Table 2.1?
questions.explanation: Plantae = tissue/organ; Fungi = multicellular loose tissue; Monera/Protista = cellular; Animalia = tissue/organ/organ system.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Chitin in the cell wall is a diagnostic Table 2.1 feature of:
questions.explanation: Only Fungi are specified as having chitinous walls in Table 2.1.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Cellulose cell wall AND photosynthetic autotrophy together identify which kingdom in Table 2.1?
questions.explanation: Plantae uniquely combines cellulose wall with exclusively photosynthetic autotrophy in the table.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: A mixotrophic unicellular eukaryote aligns best with which kingdom in Table 2.1?
questions.explanation: Protista alone among unicellular eukaryotes shows both autotrophic and heterotrophic nutrition.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The highest body organisation in Table 2.1 is seen in:
questions.explanation: Animalia alone reaches tissue/organ/organ-system level per Table 2.1.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: A filamentous photosynthetic organism with prokaryotic cells belongs in:
questions.explanation: Filamentous photosynthetic prokaryotes (cyanobacteria) are Monera.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Absence of nuclear membrane is a feature shared by Monera with:
questions.explanation: Only Monera lacks a nuclear membrane among the five kingdoms.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which kingdom shares 'Present' nuclear membrane with Fungi but differs in cell wall composition?
questions.explanation: Plantae (cellulose) and Animalia (no wall) both have nuclear membranes like Fungi but differ in wall nature.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Saprobic/parasitic heterotrophy alongside autotrophy is possible in:
questions.explanation: Monera lists both autotrophic (photo/chemo) and heterotrophic (saprophytic/parasitic) modes.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Organ-system level organisation is NOT reached by:
questions.explanation: Only Animalia reaches organ-system level; Monera, Protista are cellular; Fungi loose tissue; Plantae tissue/organ.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which kingdoms have cell walls according to Table 2.1? (Select the most complete correct set)
questions.explanation: Animalia lacks walls; Protista has walls in some; others always listed with walls.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Partial heterotrophy in insectivorous plants does NOT change their Whittaker kingdom because Table 2.1 still classifies Plantae as:
questions.option_b: Autotrophic photosynthetic eukaryotes with cellulose walls
questions.explanation: Venus fly trap and bladderwort remain in Plantae as predominantly photosynthetic with cellulose walls.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Prokaryotic cell type automatically implies which other Table 2.1 character?
questions.explanation: In Table 2.1, Monera alone is prokaryotic and alone lacks nuclear membrane.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which column in Table 2.1 is the odd one out for BOTH cell wall absence AND holozoic nutrition?
questions.explanation: Animalia alone lacks cell walls and shows holozoic heterotrophy.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Tissue/organ level body organisation with obligatory photosynthetic autotrophy identifies:
questions.explanation: Plantae = tissue/organ + photosynthetic autotrophy per Table 2.1.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Eukaryotic, chitinous wall, saprophytic/parasitic heterotrophy and loose tissue organisation collectively indicate:
questions.explanation: This combination is the Fungi column in Table 2.1.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Chlamydomonas (unicellular alga) and Spirogyra (filamentous alga) were problematic in two-kingdom classification because both were placed in:
questions.explanation: Two-kingdom Plantae lumped unicellular and multicellular photosynthetic organisms together.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Fungi were separated from plants chiefly because fungal walls contain:
questions.explanation: NCERT contrasts chitinous fungal walls with cellulosic plant walls as basis for separate kingdom.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which pair would NEVER belong to the same kingdom in Whittaker's system?
questions.explanation: Saccharomyces (yeast) is Fungi; E. coli and Nostoc are Monera; Amoeba/Euglena are Protista; Mucor/Rhizopus are Fungi.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which feature distinguishes Kingdom Fungi from Kingdom Animalia despite both being heterotrophic eukaryotes?
questions.explanation: Both lack chlorophyll and have nuclear membranes; fungi have chitinous walls, animals do not.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which kingdom is described as forming a 'link' between plants, animals and fungi?
questions.explanation: NCERT states Protista links other eukaryotic kingdoms.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Compared to Whittaker's scheme, the three-domain system splits:
questions.explanation: Three-domain system divides Monera (prokaryotes) into two domains; eukaryotes form the third.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Unicellularity in Whittaker's system does NOT automatically place an organism in Protista because:
questions.option_a: Yeast are fungi and bacteria are monerans
questions.explanation: Unicellular eukaryotes are mostly Protista, but yeast (Fungi) and bacteria (Monera) are exceptions.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Cuscuta and Venus fly trap both belong to Plantae but differ in mode of partial heterotrophy as:
questions.explanation: Cuscuta is a plant parasite; Venus fly trap is insectivorous—both partially heterotrophic plants.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Fungi and many Moneran heterotrophs both exhibit saprophytic nutrition, but differ in:
questions.explanation: Both can be saprophytic heterotrophs; fungi are eukaryotic with chitin walls, monerans prokaryotic.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which protistan group is most closely allied to Kingdom Animalia by NCERT description?
questions.explanation: NCERT calls protozoans primitive relatives of animals; they were historically placed in Animalia.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Slime moulds resemble fungi in spore formation but differ from true fungi because slime moulds:
questions.option_b: Are saprophytic protists with plasmodium stage, not chitinous hyphal fungi
questions.explanation: Slime moulds are protists with plasmodium/fruiting body spores; fungi have chitinous hyphae.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Algae appear in both Plantae (Chapter 3) and Protista (Chapter 2) discussions because:
questions.option_a: Classification boundaries of some algae remain debated; unicellular forms may be treated as protists
questions.explanation: NCERT notes Protista boundaries are not well defined; what is a protistan alga to one biologist may be a plant to another.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which Whittaker kingdom alone shows organ-system level organisation and neuromotor elaboration per NCERT?
questions.explanation: Animalia: tissue/organ/organ-system, locomotion, sensory and neuromotor mechanisms.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Alternation of generations is a feature of Kingdom Plantae but NOT of:
questions.option_c: Both Fungi and Animalia as described in this chapter
questions.explanation: Chapter 2 introduces alternation of generations for Plantae; Animalia has diploid soma with separate gametes; fungal life cycles differ.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Mycorrhiza and lichens both involve fungi, but mycorrhiza partners:
questions.explanation: Mycorrhiza = fungus + plant roots; lichen = fungus + alga.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Refrigeration retards fungal and bacterial growth primarily because these organisms prefer:
questions.explanation: NCERT notes fungi prefer warm humid places; refrigeration reduces growth of microbes on food.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: All of the following are bacterial shapes mentioned in NCERT EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Four shapes: coccus, bacillus, vibrio, spirillum. Trichome is a filament arrangement, not a shape category here.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: All of the following are archaebacterial groups EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Cyanobacteria are eubacteria (photosynthetic), not archaebacteria.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: All of the following are protozoan groups in NCERT EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Euglenoids are a separate protistan group, not one of the four protozoan subgroups.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: All of the following are fungal classes in Chapter 2 EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: NCERT lists Phycomycetes, Ascomycetes, Basidiomycetes, Deuteromycetes—not Zygomycota by that name.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: All of the following are viral diseases per NCERT EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Sleeping sickness is caused by Trypanosoma (protozoan), not a virus.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: All of the following are phycomycetes examples EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Penicillium is an ascomycete (sac-fungus), not phycomycete.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: All of the following are basidiomycetes EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Aspergillus is an ascomycete; Agaricus, Ustilago (smut) and Puccinia (rust) are basidiomycetes.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: All of the following are acellular or non-five-kingdom entities in NCERT EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Euglena is a protist; viruses, viroids and prions are outside five kingdom classification.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: All are economically important roles of heterotrophic bacteria EXCEPT:
questions.option_d: Production of biogas methane in cattle rumen
questions.explanation: Methane in cattle rumen is produced by methanogenic archaebacteria, not heterotrophic eubacteria roles listed.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: All of the following are fungal vegetative reproductive modes EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: NCERT lists fragmentation, fission and budding for fungi vegetatively; bacterial binary fission is prokaryotic.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: All of the following are steps in fungal sexual cycle EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Fungal sexual cycle involves plasmogamy, karyogamy and meiosis producing haploid spores—not binary fission of zygote.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Rapid multiplication of Gonyaulax in seawater leads to:
questions.option_b: Red tides toxic to marine life
questions.explanation: Red dinoflagellates like Gonyaulax cause red tides releasing toxins killing fish.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Trypanosoma belongs to which protistan category and causes:
questions.explanation: Trypanosoma is a flagellated protozoan causing sleeping sickness.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Plasmodium is classified as a:
questions.explanation: Plasmodium is placed among sporozoans with an infectious spore-like stage.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Neurospora is favoured in laboratories because it is:
questions.option_b: An ascomycete used in biochemical and genetic studies
questions.explanation: Neurospora is an ascomycete model organism for genetics.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Saccharomyces cerevisiae is taxonomically an:
questions.explanation: Yeast (Saccharomyces) is placed under Ascomycetes (rarely unicellular).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Euglena differs from true plants because it possesses:
questions.option_a: Pellicle instead of cellulosic wall and shows mixotrophy
questions.explanation: Euglenoids have protein-rich pellicle, not cellulose wall, and can become heterotrophic.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Paramoecium moves and feeds using:
questions.option_b: Thousands of cilia and a gullet
questions.explanation: Paramoecium is ciliated with coordinated ciliary movement steering food into gullet.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Entamoeba histolytica is an example of:
questions.explanation: Entamoeba is listed among amoeboid protozoans including parasitic forms.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Puccinia is a basidiomycete causing:
questions.explanation: Puccinia is the rust fungus; Ustilago causes smut.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Ustilago is grouped with Puccinia under:
questions.explanation: Both Ustilago (smut) and Puccinia (rust) are basidiomycetes.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Aspergillus produces conidia exogenously on:
questions.explanation: Ascomycetes bear exogenous conidia on specialised conidiophores.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Nostoc is a filamentous member of:
questions.explanation: Nostoc is a nitrogen-fixing cyanobacterium (blue-green alga) in Monera.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The scientist associated with 'Contagium vivum fluidum' is:
questions.explanation: Beijerinck (1898) coined virus and called the infectious fluid Contagium vivum fluidum.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Potato spindle tuber disease is linked to discovery of:
questions.explanation: Diener (1971) discovered viroids as causal agents of potato spindle tuber disease.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Under unfavourable conditions bacteria may reproduce by:
questions.option_a: Spore formation and primitive DNA transfer between cells
questions.explanation: Besides fission, bacteria form spores under stress and show primitive sexual DNA transfer.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Nitrifying bacteria in soil contribute primarily to:
questions.option_a: Nitrogen cycling via oxidation of nitrogenous compounds
questions.explanation: Chemosynthetic autotrophs oxidise inorganic nitrogen compounds and recycle soil nitrogen.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Mycoplasma can survive without oxygen and lack:
questions.explanation: Mycoplasma completely lack cell walls and many are anaerobic pathogens.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: An 'algal bloom' in polluted freshwater is most likely due to excessive growth of:
questions.explanation: NCERT links cyanobacterial blooms to polluted water bodies (exercise concept: algal bloom).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which archaebacterial group would dominate in the Great Salt Lake-type environment?
questions.explanation: Halophiles inhabit extreme salinity; methanogens marshy/rumen; thermoacidophiles hot acidic springs.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Archaebacteria in Yellowstone-type hot acidic springs are:
questions.explanation: Thermoacidophiles colonise hot spring habitats per NCERT.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Motility in eubacteria is commonly associated with:
questions.explanation: Eubacteria character includes flagellum when motile; cilia/pseudopodia are eukaryotic.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Rhizobium-type nitrogen fixation in legume roots is an example of beneficial:
questions.explanation: NCERT cites heterotrophic bacteria fixing nitrogen in legume roots among useful roles.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Photosynthetic autotrophy in bacteria is represented by:
questions.option_a: Cyanobacteria (oxygenic) and some without oxygen release
questions.explanation: Cyanobacteria are photosynthetic autotrophs with chlorophyll a; bacteria also include chemosynthetic and heterotrophic forms.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Psychrophilic survival in snow is a trait of:
questions.explanation: NCERT notes bacteria inhabit extreme cold including snow.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The transverse flagellum in dinoflagellates lies in:
questions.option_a: A furrow between cellulose wall plates
questions.explanation: Dinoflagellates have stiff cellulose plates; one flagellum lies transversely in the inter-plate furrow.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Indestructibility of diatom walls is due to:
questions.explanation: Diatom walls (frustules) are silica-embedded, resisting decay.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Desmids are grouped with diatoms under:
questions.explanation: Chrysophytes include diatoms and golden algae (desmids).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: When sunlight is available Euglenoids are:
questions.explanation: Euglenoids photosynthesise in light using plant-like pigments.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The plasmodium stage in slime moulds is:
questions.explanation: Plasmodium is a spreading saprophytic mass formed under suitable conditions.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Silica shells on marine amoeboid protozoans distinguish them from:
questions.explanation: NCERT notes marine amoeboids may bear silica shells; freshwater Amoeba uses pseudopodia without such shells.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: A free-living vs parasitic distinction applies to which protozoan group?
questions.explanation: Flagellated protozoans include free-living forms and parasites like Trypanosoma.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The spore-like infectious stage is characteristic of:
questions.explanation: Sporozoans are defined by an infectious spore-like life-cycle stage.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Sexual reproduction in protists involves:
questions.option_a: Cell fusion followed by zygote formation
questions.explanation: Protists reproduce sexually via cell fusion and zygote formation per NCERT.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Passive floating of chrysophytes in water currents defines them as part of:
questions.explanation: Microscopic passively floating photosynthetic chrysophytes are plankton (chief ocean producers include diatoms).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Motile asexual spores in phycomycetes are:
questions.explanation: Phycomycetes produce motile zoospores or non-motile aplanospores in sporangia.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Isogamous, anisogamous or oogamous fusion in phycomycetes produces:
questions.explanation: Phycomycete sexual reproduction culminates in a zygospore from gamete fusion.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Coenocytic hyphae in phycomycetes means:
questions.explanation: Aseptate coenocytic hyphae are continuous tubes with many nuclei.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Ascocarps are:
questions.option_a: Fruiting bodies bearing asci with ascospores
questions.explanation: Asci are arranged in ascocarps—fruiting bodies of ascomycetes.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: In basidiomycetes plasmogamy occurs between:
questions.option_a: Two vegetative/somatic cells of different mating types
questions.explanation: Basidiomycetes lack sex organs; compatible hyphal cells fuse (plasmogamy).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Vegetative reproduction common in basidiomycetes is:
questions.explanation: Basidiomycetes typically lack asexual spores; fragmentation is common vegetatively.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: When sexual stage of a deuteromycete is discovered it is often reclassified into:
questions.explanation: Perfect stages of imperfect fungi are moved to ascomycetes or basidiomycetes upon discovery.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Edible delicacies morels and truffles belong to:
questions.explanation: NCERT lists morels and truffles as edible ascomycete members.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Coprophilous habit is mentioned for:
questions.explanation: Ascomycetes include coprophilous (dung-growing) forms among saprobes and parasites.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Reduction division in basidiomycete fruiting bodies produces:
questions.explanation: Karyogamy and meiosis in basidium yield four haploid basidiospores externally.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Ivanowsky (1892) demonstrated that TMV causative agents are:
questions.explanation: Filter-passage showed TMV pathogen smaller than bacteria.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Stanley's 1935 crystallisation of viruses proved they contain largely:
questions.explanation: Stanley showed viruses crystallise as largely protein; they are nucleoproteins with RNA or DNA.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which statement about viral nucleic acid is INCORRECT?
questions.option_a: A single virus particle may contain both DNA and RNA
questions.option_b: Animal viruses may have ss/ds RNA or ds DNA
questions.explanation: NCERT clearly states no virus contains both RNA and DNA in the same particle.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: A lichen-free tree trunk in an industrial city suggests:
questions.explanation: Lichens are sensitive pollution indicators and fail to grow in polluted air—applied NEET concept.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which of the following groups are described under Kingdom Plantae in this chapter?
questions.explanation: Chapter 3 covers Algae, Bryophytes, Pteridophytes, Gymnosperms and Angiosperms under Plantae.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which groups have been excluded from Kingdom Plantae in modern classification?
questions.explanation: Fungi and members of Monera and Protista with cell walls are no longer placed in Plantae.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Why are cyanobacteria (blue-green algae) no longer classified as algae?
questions.option_b: They are excluded from Plantae and placed in Monera
questions.explanation: Cyanobacteria belong to Kingdom Monera and are excluded from Plantae; hence they are not considered true algae.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Linnaeus's classification system was based mainly on:
questions.explanation: Linnaeus used vegetative characters or androecium structure; such artificial systems gave equal weight to easily modified vegetative traits.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Natural classification of flowering plants was given by:
questions.option_b: George Bentham and Joseph Dalton Hooker
questions.explanation: Bentham and Hooker developed a natural classification based on affinities, internal features, anatomy, embryology and phytochemistry.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Phylogenetic classification assumes that organisms in the same taxa:
questions.explanation: Phylogenetic systems group organisms based on evolutionary relationships, assuming a common ancestor for members of the same taxon.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Numerical Taxonomy is characterised by:
questions.option_b: Considering all observable characteristics with equal importance
questions.explanation: Numerical Taxonomy assigns codes to all observable characters and processes them by computer, giving each character equal weight.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Cytotaxonomy is based on:
questions.option_b: Cytological information like chromosome number, structure and behaviour
questions.explanation: Cytotaxonomy uses cytological data; chemotaxonomy uses chemical constituents of plants to resolve classification difficulties.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which set of features correctly describes algae?
questions.explanation: Algae are chlorophyll-bearing, simple, thalloid, autotrophic organisms found mainly in aquatic habitats.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Algae may be found in association with:
questions.option_b: Fungi (lichens) and animals such as on sloth bear
questions.explanation: Besides aquatic and moist habitats, algae occur on moist stones, soils, wood, in lichens (with fungi), and on animals like sloth bear.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Volvox represents which type of algal body form?
questions.explanation: Volvox is a colonial alga; Ulothrix and Spirogyra are filamentous forms.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Kelps are examples of algae that:
questions.explanation: Kelps are marine brown algae that form very large, massive plant bodies.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Vegetative reproduction in algae typically occurs by:
questions.explanation: In algae, vegetative reproduction is by fragmentation; each fragment develops into a new thallus.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Zoospores in algae are:
questions.explanation: Zoospores are the most common asexual spores in algae; they are flagellated, motile, and germinate into new plants.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Fusion of gametes dissimilar in size, as in Eudorina, is called:
questions.explanation: Anisogamy involves fusion of two gametes of unequal size; isogamy involves similar-sized gametes; oogamy involves a large non-motile egg and small motile male gamete.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Oogamous reproduction is exemplified by:
questions.explanation: Oogamy involves a large non-motile female gamete and a smaller motile male gamete; examples include Volvox and Fucus.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Approximately what fraction of total global CO₂ fixation is carried out by algae?
questions.explanation: Algae carry out at least half of the total carbon dioxide fixation on Earth through photosynthesis.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which marine algae are used as food?
questions.option_b: Porphyra, Laminaria and Sargassum among others
questions.explanation: About 70 species of marine algae are used as food, including Porphyra, Laminaria and Sargassum.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Algin and carrageen are hydrocolloids obtained respectively from:
questions.explanation: Algin is obtained from brown algae; carrageen is obtained from red algae. Both are commercially important hydrocolloids.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Agar used for growing microbes is obtained from:
questions.explanation: Agar is a commercial product from Gelidium and Gracilaria (red algae), used in microbiological media and food preparations.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Chlorella is valued as a food supplement because it is:
questions.option_a: A multicellular brown alga rich in lipids
questions.option_b: A unicellular alga rich in proteins
questions.option_c: A red alga rich in floridean starch
questions.explanation: Chlorella is a unicellular green alga rich in proteins, used even as food supplement by space travellers.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The three main classes of algae are:
questions.explanation: Algae are classified into Chlorophyceae (green), Phaeophyceae (brown) and Rhodophyceae (red algae).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Members of Chlorophyceae are commonly called:
questions.explanation: Chlorophyceae are the green algae, grass-green due to chlorophyll a and b.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The dominant pigments in Chlorophyceae are:
questions.option_c: Chlorophyll a and c with fucoxanthin
questions.explanation: Green algae appear grass green due to dominance of chlorophyll a and b.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Pyrenoids in green algae contain:
questions.explanation: Pyrenoids are storage bodies in chloroplasts of green algae; they contain protein in addition to starch.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The cell wall of green algae consists of:
questions.explanation: Green algae have a rigid cell wall with an inner cellulose layer and outer pectose layer.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which of the following is a green alga?
questions.explanation: Spirogyra is a green alga (Chlorophyceae); Fucus is brown, Porphyra and Polysiphonia are red algae.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Brown algae (Phaeophyceae) are found primarily in:
questions.explanation: Phaeophyceae or brown algae occur primarily in marine habitats.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Kelps, brown algae, may reach a height of:
questions.explanation: Kelps are profusely branched brown algae that may reach heights of about 100 metres.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The brown colour of Phaeophyceae is mainly due to:
questions.explanation: Brown algae vary from olive green to brown shades depending on the amount of fucoxanthin, a xanthophyll pigment.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Food reserve in brown algae is stored as:
questions.explanation: Brown algae store food as complex carbohydrates—laminarin or mannitol.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: In brown algae, the leaf-like photosynthetic organ is called:
questions.explanation: Brown algal body has holdfast, stipe (stalk), and frond (leaf-like photosynthetic organ).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Zoospores of brown algae characteristically have:
questions.explanation: Brown algal zoospores are biflagellate, pear-shaped, with two unequal laterally attached flagella.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which of the following is a brown alga?
questions.explanation: Laminaria is a brown alga; Ulothrix and Chara are green algae; Porphyra is a red alga.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The red colour of Rhodophyceae is due to predominance of:
questions.explanation: Red algae owe their colour to predominance of r-phycoerythrin.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Food reserve in red algae is:
questions.explanation: Red algae store food as floridean starch, structurally similar to amylopectin and glycogen.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Red algae characteristically reproduce asexually and sexually using:
questions.explanation: Red algae produce non-motile spores asexually and non-motile gametes sexually.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Sexual reproduction in red algae is:
questions.explanation: Red algae show oogamous sexual reproduction accompanied by complex post-fertilisation developments.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which of the following is a red alga?
questions.explanation: Porphyra is a red alga; Polysiphonia, Gracilaria and Gelidium are also red algae.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: According to Table 3.1, stored food in Chlorophyceae is:
questions.explanation: Table 3.1 lists starch as the stored food in Chlorophyceae (green algae).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Flagella in Chlorophyceae are described as:
questions.explanation: Table 3.1 states Chlorophyceae have 2-8 equal, apically inserted flagella.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: According to Table 3.1, major pigments in Phaeophyceae include:
questions.explanation: Table 3.1 lists chlorophyll a, c and fucoxanthin as major pigments of brown algae.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Cell wall composition of Phaeophyceae according to Table 3.1 is:
questions.explanation: Brown algae have cell walls of cellulose and algin as per Table 3.1.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: According to Table 3.1, flagella in Rhodophyceae are:
questions.explanation: Table 3.1 indicates flagella are absent in Rhodophyceae (red algae).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Major pigments of Rhodophyceae listed in Table 3.1 are:
questions.explanation: Table 3.1 lists chlorophyll a, d and phycoerythrin as major pigments of red algae.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Habitat of Rhodophyceae according to Table 3.1 is predominantly:
questions.option_c: Salt water (most), with some in fresh and brackish water
questions.explanation: Table 3.1 shows Rhodophyceae occur in fresh water (some), brackish water, and mostly in salt water.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Bryophytes are called 'amphibians of the plant kingdom' because they:
questions.option_b: Can live in soil but need water for sexual reproduction
questions.explanation: Bryophytes live on soil but require water for sexual reproduction, hence the amphibian analogy.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Bryophytes are ecologically important in:
questions.option_b: Plant succession on bare rocks and soil
questions.explanation: Bryophytes play a key role in plant succession on bare rocks and soil.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Bryophytes lack:
questions.explanation: Bryophytes lack true roots, stems and leaves but may have root-like, leaf-like or stem-like structures.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The dominant, gamete-producing body of bryophytes is the:
questions.explanation: The main plant body of bryophytes is haploid and produces gametes; it is called the gametophyte.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Antherozoids produced in bryophyte antheridia are:
questions.explanation: Antheridia produce biflagellate antherozoids (male gametes) in bryophytes.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The archegonium in bryophytes:
questions.option_b: Is flask-shaped and produces a single egg
questions.explanation: Archegonium is the female sex organ; it is flask-shaped and produces a single egg.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The bryophyte sporophyte:
questions.option_b: Is attached to and nourished by the gametophyte
questions.explanation: Bryophyte sporophyte is dependent on the photosynthetic gametophyte for nourishment and is not free-living.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Sphagnum moss is economically useful because it:
questions.option_b: Provides peat used as fuel and water-holding packing material
questions.explanation: Sphagnum provides peat used as fuel and as packing material due to its high water-holding capacity.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Mosses and lichens are ecologically important as:
questions.explanation: Mosses and lichens are pioneer colonisers of rocks, initiating soil formation.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Dense moss mats help prevent soil erosion by:
questions.option_b: Reducing impact of falling rain on soil
questions.explanation: Moss mats reduce rain impact on soil and help prevent erosion.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Marchantia, a liverwort, has a plant body that is:
questions.option_c: Differentiated into true root, stem and leaf
questions.explanation: Marchantia has a thalloid, dorsiventral body closely appressed to the substrate.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Gemmae in liverworts are:
questions.option_b: Green multicellular asexual buds in gemma cups
questions.explanation: Gemmae are green, multicellular asexual buds formed in gemma cups on liverwort thalli.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Liverwort sporophyte is differentiated into:
questions.explanation: Liverwort sporophyte has foot, seta and capsule; spores form in the capsule after meiosis.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The predominant stage in moss life cycle is:
questions.option_b: Gametophyte with protonema and leafy stages
questions.explanation: Moss life cycle is gametophyte-dominant, with protonema and leafy gametophyte stages.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Protonema in mosses is:
questions.option_b: A creeping, green, branched filamentous stage from spore
questions.explanation: Protonema develops directly from spore; it is creeping, green, branched and often filamentous.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Rhizoids in the leafy stage of mosses are:
questions.explanation: The leafy moss gametophyte is attached by multicellular, branched rhizoids.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Compared to liverworts, moss sporophytes are:
questions.explanation: Moss sporophytes are more elaborate than liverwort sporophytes.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which of the following is a moss?
questions.explanation: Funaria is a moss; Marchantia is a liverwort; Selaginella is a pteridophyte; Cycas is a gymnosperm.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Pteridophytes include:
questions.explanation: Pteridophytes include horsetails (e.g., Equisetum) and ferns.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Pteridophytes are the first terrestrial plants to possess:
questions.explanation: Pteridophytes are the first terrestrial plants with vascular tissues—xylem and phloem.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: In pteridophytes, the dominant plant body is the:
questions.option_b: Sporophyte differentiated into true root, stem and leaves
questions.explanation: Unlike bryophytes, pteridophytes have a dominant sporophyte with true roots, stems and leaves.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Microphylls are found in:
questions.explanation: Selaginella has small leaves called microphylls; ferns have large macrophylls.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Leaf-like appendages bearing sporangia in pteridophytes are called:
questions.explanation: Sporangia in pteridophytes are borne on sporophylls—leaf-like appendages on the sporophyte.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Strobili or cones in pteridophytes are formed in:
questions.explanation: Sporophylls may form compact strobili or cones, as in Selaginella and Equisetum.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The gametophyte of pteridophytes is called:
questions.explanation: Pteridophyte spores germinate into a free-living, photosynthetic thalloid gametophyte called prothallus.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: In pteridophytes, fertilisation requires:
questions.option_b: Water for transfer of antherozoids to archegonium
questions.explanation: Water is needed to carry antherozoids from antheridia to the archegonium in pteridophytes.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Majority of pteridophytes are:
questions.explanation: Most pteridophytes produce spores of one kind and are homosporous.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Heterosporous pteridophytes include:
questions.explanation: Selaginella and Salvinia produce macro and micro spores and are heterosporous.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Retention of female gametophyte and embryo development on sporophyte in heterosporous pteridophytes is a precursor to:
questions.explanation: Heterospory with retained female gametophyte and embryo on sporophyte foreshadows the seed habit.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Equisetum belongs to the pteridophyte class:
questions.explanation: Equisetum (horsetail) belongs to Sphenopsida; Selaginella is Lycopsida; Dryopteris is Pteropsida.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Gymnosperms are so named because their:
questions.option_b: Seeds are naked (not enclosed in fruit)
questions.explanation: Gymnos means naked; gymnosperm seeds are not covered by ovary wall or fruit.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: One of the tallest tree species among gymnosperms is:
questions.explanation: Sequoia, a giant redwood gymnosperm, is among the tallest tree species.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Mycorrhizal association is seen in roots of:
questions.explanation: Pinus roots have mycorrhizal fungal association; Cycas has coralloid roots with N₂-fixing cyanobacteria.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: In Cycas, leaves are:
questions.option_b: Pinnate and persist for a few years
questions.explanation: Cycas has pinnate leaves that persist for several years; conifers have needle-like leaves.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Needle-like leaves of conifers help reduce water loss by:
questions.option_b: Reducing surface area along with thick cuticle and sunken stomata
questions.option_c: Producing more stomata on upper surface
questions.explanation: Conifer needles reduce surface area; thick cuticle and sunken stomata further reduce transpiration.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Gymnosperms are:
questions.explanation: Gymnosperms produce microspores and megaspores and are heterosporous.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The reduced male gametophyte of gymnosperms is the:
questions.explanation: Microspores develop into a highly reduced male gametophyte called the pollen grain.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: In which gymnosperm are male and female cones borne on the same tree?
questions.option_c: Both Cycas and Pinus on separate trees only
questions.explanation: Pinus bears male and female cones on the same tree; in Cycas, male cones and megasporophylls are on different trees.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: In gymnosperms, nucellus protected by envelopes forms the:
questions.explanation: Ovule consists of nucellus protected by envelopes; ovules are borne on megasporophylls.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: In gymnosperms, gametophytes:
questions.option_b: Remain within sporangia on sporophyte without free-living existence
questions.explanation: Gymnosperm gametophytes are retained within sporangia on the sporophyte and are not free-living.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Fertilisation in gymnosperms involves:
questions.option_b: Pollen tube delivering male gametes to archegonia in ovules
questions.explanation: Pollen grains form pollen tubes that grow to archegonia in ovules to deliver male gametes.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: In angiosperms, pollen grains and ovules develop in:
questions.explanation: Angiosperms produce pollen grains and ovules within specialised structures called flowers.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: A key difference between angiosperms and gymnosperms is that angiosperm seeds are:
questions.explanation: Angiosperm seeds are enclosed in fruits; gymnosperm seeds remain naked.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The smallest angiosperm mentioned in the chapter is:
questions.explanation: Wolffia is among the smallest angiosperms; Eucalyptus trees exceed 100 metres in height.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Angiosperms are divided into:
questions.explanation: Angiosperms comprise two classes: dicotyledons and monocotyledons.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Isogamous reproduction is seen in:
questions.explanation: Isogamy involves similar-sized gametes, as in Ulothrix (flagellated) and Spirogyra (non-flagellated motile).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Ribbon-shaped chloroplasts are characteristic of:
questions.explanation: Green algae show varied chloroplast shapes; Spirogyra is well known for spiral/ribbon-shaped chloroplasts.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Red algae are predominantly:
questions.explanation: Majority of red algae are marine, with greater concentrations in warmer areas.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Red algae can grow:
questions.option_b: Both near surface and at great depths with little light
questions.explanation: Red algae occur in well-lit surface waters and at ocean depths where little light penetrates.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Bryophytes are commonly found in:
questions.explanation: Mosses and liverworts commonly grow in moist, shaded habitats, especially in hilly regions.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Bryophytes are divided into:
questions.explanation: Bryophytes comprise liverworts and mosses.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Pteridophytes are typically found in:
questions.explanation: Pteridophytes typically inhabit cool, damp, shady places; some grow in sandy soils.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Pteridophytes are useful as:
questions.explanation: Pteridophytes serve medicinal purposes, act as soil-binders, and are grown as ornamentals.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Male cones in gymnosperms are also called:
questions.explanation: Strobili with microsporophylls and microsporangia are microsporangiate (male) strobili.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: After fertilisation in gymnosperms, ovules develop into:
questions.explanation: In gymnosperms, fertilised ovules develop into seeds that remain naked (uncovered).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Photosynthetic algae benefit aquatic environments by:
questions.explanation: Photosynthetic algae increase dissolved oxygen levels in their immediate aquatic environment.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: In Chlorophyceae, asexual reproduction occurs through:
questions.explanation: Green algae reproduce asexually by flagellated zoospores produced in zoosporangia.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Brown algae possess which chlorophyll types?
questions.explanation: Phaeophyceae have chlorophyll a and c, along with carotenoids and xanthophylls including fucoxanthin.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Female gametophyte of gymnosperms develops from:
questions.explanation: One megaspore develops into the multicellular female gametophyte bearing archegonia inside the megasporangium.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Chemotaxonomy utilises:
questions.explanation: Chemotaxonomy uses chemical constituents of plants to resolve taxonomic confusions.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: According to Table 3.1, which algal class stores food as floridean starch and lacks flagella?
questions.explanation: Rhodophyceae store floridean starch and have absent flagella per Table 3.1.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Fucoxanthin masks the green colour in brown algae because it:
questions.option_b: Predominates over chlorophyll and carotenoids in amount
questions.explanation: High fucoxanthin content gives Phaeophyceae their brown appearance.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Isogamy in algae is exemplified by Ulothrix and Spirogyra. The key feature of isogamy is:
questions.option_c: Fusion of large static female and small motile male gamete
questions.explanation: Isogamy involves fusion of gametes similar in morphology/size.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: A student observes non-motile spores and non-motile gametes in an alga. The alga is most likely:
questions.explanation: Rhodophyceae like Polysiphonia have non-motile spores and gametes.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which of the following statements about algae is INCORRECT?
questions.option_a: Algae are largely aquatic, chlorophyll-bearing autotrophs
questions.option_b: Cyanobacteria are true members of Chlorophyceae
questions.option_c: Algae may occur on moist stones, soils and wood
questions.option_d: Some algae form associations with fungi as lichens
questions.explanation: Cyanobacteria (blue-green algae) are in Monera, not true algae.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which of the following is an INCORRECT comparison between bryophytes and pteridophytes?
questions.option_a: Bryophytes — gametophyte dominant; Pteridophytes — sporophyte dominant
questions.option_b: Bryophytes — no true vascular tissue; Pteridophytes — xylem and phloem present
questions.option_c: Bryophytes — sporophyte free-living; Pteridophytes — sporophyte dependent on gametophyte
questions.explanation: In bryophytes sporophyte is dependent; in pteridophytes sporophyte is independent dominant plant.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Archegonium is a flask-shaped multicellular structure that produces:
questions.explanation: Archegonium produces a single egg; antheridium produces biflagellate antherozoids.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Gemma cups containing gemmae for asexual reproduction are found in:
questions.explanation: Liverworts like Marchantia produce gemmae in gemma cups on thalli.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The upright leafy gametophore of moss develops from protonema as:
questions.option_b: A lateral bud from secondary protonema
questions.explanation: Leafy stage develops as lateral bud from secondary protonema.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The inconspicuous prothallus of ferns requires cool, damp, shady habitats because it:
questions.option_b: Is a photosynthetic gametophyte needing moisture for growth and fertilisation
questions.explanation: Prothallus is haploid gametophyte needing damp conditions and water for fertilisation.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Retention of female gametophyte on sporophyte and embryo development within it in heterosporous pteridophytes represents:
questions.explanation: This retention and embryo development foreshadows the seed habit in gymnosperms.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: In gymnosperms, ovules remain exposed because they are NOT enclosed by:
questions.explanation: Gymnosperm ovules lack ovary wall; hence seeds are naked.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Gymnosperms and angiosperms both produce seeds yet are separate groups because:
questions.option_b: Gymnosperm seeds are naked; angiosperm seeds are enclosed in fruit
questions.explanation: Seed enclosure in fruit (angiosperms) vs naked seeds (gymnosperms) is the key distinction.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: In gymnosperms, the male gametophyte is represented by:
questions.explanation: Highly reduced male gametophyte of gymnosperms is the pollen grain.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Dioecious condition (male and female structures on different trees) is seen in:
questions.explanation: In Cycas, male cones and megasporophylls are on different trees.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Monoecious gymnosperm with male and female cones on the same tree:
questions.explanation: Pinus bears microsporangiate and megasporangiate cones on same tree.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which of the following statements about gymnosperms is INCORRECT?
questions.option_b: Seeds develop from fertilised ovules but remain naked
questions.option_c: Ovules are enclosed within a fruit developed from ovary
questions.explanation: Gymnosperms lack ovary; ovules and seeds are not enclosed in fruit.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Meiosis (reduction division) in bryophytes occurs in cells of the:
questions.explanation: In bryophytes, meiosis occurs in sporophyte spore mother cells within capsule.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The ploidy of protonemal cell of a moss is:
questions.explanation: Protonema is part of haploid gametophyte generation in moss.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Gemma cell in Marchantia is:
questions.explanation: Gemmae are multicellular asexual buds on haploid gametophytic thallus.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Female gametophyte in gymnosperms develops from:
questions.explanation: One megaspore develops into multicellular female gametophyte within megasporangium.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question:
Match Column I with Column II:
Column I: (a) Chlamydomonas (b) Cycas (c) Selaginella (d) Sphagnum
Column II: (i) Moss (ii) Pteridophyte (iii) Algae (iv) Gymnosperm
questions.explanation: Chlamydomonas (algae), Cycas (gymnosperm), Selaginella (pteridophyte), Sphagnum (moss).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Volvox exhibits oogamous reproduction and body organisation as:
questions.explanation: Volvox is colonial green alga showing oogamous reproduction.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Gelidium and Gracilaria used for agar production belong to:
questions.explanation: Gelidium and Gracilaria are red algae (Rhodophyceae) yielding agar.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Carrageen is a hydrocolloid obtained from:
questions.explanation: Carrageen is commercial hydrocolloid from red algae; algin from brown algae.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which of the following statements about red algae is INCORRECT?
questions.option_c: Asexual reproduction by motile zoospores with flagella
questions.explanation: Red algae reproduce asexually by non-motile spores; flagella are absent.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which of the following statements about brown algae is INCORRECT?
questions.option_b: Store food as laminarin or mannitol
questions.option_d: Zoospores are biflagellate with unequal lateral flagella
questions.explanation: Phaeophyceae are primarily marine, not predominantly fresh water.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which of the following statements about bryophytes is INCORRECT?
questions.option_c: They possess true roots, stems and leaves
questions.explanation: Bryophytes lack true roots, stems and leaves; they have root-like/leaf-like structures.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which of the following statements about pteridophytes is INCORRECT?
questions.option_a: First terrestrial plants with vascular tissue
questions.option_c: Prothallus is the dominant independent plant body
questions.explanation: Prothallus is inconspicuous gametophyte; sporophyte is dominant in pteridophytes.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which of the following statements about angiosperms is INCORRECT?
questions.option_d: Pollen and ovules develop in flowers
questions.explanation: Angiosperm seeds are enclosed in fruits, not naked.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Cytotaxonomy utilises information from:
questions.explanation: Cytotaxonomy is based on cytological/chromosomal data.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Chemotaxonomy helps resolve classification problems using:
questions.explanation: Chemotaxonomy uses chemical constituents for taxonomic resolution.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Unbranched stem is characteristic of gymnosperm genus:
questions.explanation: Cycas has unbranched stem; Pinus and Cedrus have branched stems.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Bryophytes and lichens are pioneer colonisers on bare rocks because they:
questions.option_b: Help decompose rock and prepare substrate for higher plants
questions.explanation: Mosses and lichens colonise rocks and decompose them for succession.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Sphagnum moss is economically important primarily for:
questions.option_b: Peat formation, water retention and packing material
questions.explanation: Sphagnum forms peat (fuel), holds water for packing trans-shipped living material.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Dorsiventral thallus appressed to substrate is characteristic of:
questions.explanation: Marchantia liverwort has dorsiventral thalloid body.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Leafy liverworts differ from thalloid liverworts by having:
questions.option_b: Two rows of leaf-like appendages on stem-like axis
questions.explanation: Leafy liverworts have tiny leaves in two rows on stem-like structures.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Salvinia is a heterosporous pteridophyte that is:
questions.explanation: Salvinia is heterosporous aquatic pteridophyte (listed in Figure 3.3).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Adiantum (maidenhair fern) belongs to pteridophyte class:
questions.explanation: Adiantum, Dryopteris, Pteris are Pteropsida (ferns).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Psilotum is the representative genus of class:
questions.explanation: Psilotum represents Psilopsida among pteridophyte classes.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Heterospory is significant in plant evolution because it leads to:
questions.explanation: Heterospory (Selaginella, Salvinia, gymnosperms) is step toward seed habit.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: A diplontic life cycle (dominant diploid sporophyte, gametophyte reduced) is best represented by:
questions.explanation: Gymnosperms/angiosperms show diplontic trend with reduced gametophytes.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Sporophylls are leaf-like structures that:
questions.option_a: Bear sporangia and may form strobili
questions.explanation: Sporophylls bear sporangia; in some pteridophytes they form strobili/cones.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Red algae differ from brown algae in that red algae have:
questions.explanation: Rhodophyceae lack flagella and have non-motile gametes; Phaeophyceae have motile gametes.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Mosses differ from liverworts because mosses have:
questions.option_b: Protonema stage and more elaborate sporophyte
questions.explanation: Mosses show protonema and leafy stage; sporophyte more elaborate than liverworts.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Homosporous pteridophytes differ from heterosporous ones because homosporous plants produce:
questions.explanation: Homosporous = single spore type; heterosporous = macro- and microspores.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: In bryophytes, immediately after zygote formation:
questions.option_b: Zygote develops into multicellular sporophyte without immediate meiosis
questions.explanation: Bryophyte zygote does not reduce immediately; it develops into sporophyte first.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: In heterosporous pteridophytes, female gametophyte is:
questions.option_b: Retained on parent sporophyte for variable periods
questions.explanation: Female gametophyte retained on sporophyte in heterosporous pteridophytes.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: In oogamous brown algae, fertilisation may occur:
