questions.option_a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.option_b: Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
questions.option_c: A is true but R is false
questions.option_d: A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both true; R explains exine resistance.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Assertion (A): Tapetal cells nourish developing microspores. Reason (R): Tapetum is the innermost wall layer of microsporangium. Choose the correct option:
questions.option_a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.option_b: Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
questions.option_c: A is true but R is false
questions.option_d: A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both true; R identifies nourishing layer.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Assertion (A): Anther and stigma at different positions discourage self-pollination. Reason (R): This device is called herkogamy. Choose the correct option:
questions.option_a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.option_b: Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
questions.option_c: A is true but R is false
questions.option_d: A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both true; spatial separation = herkogamy.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Assertion (A): Pollen release and stigma receptivity may be non-synchronous. Reason (R): This prevents autogamy in some species. Choose the correct option:
questions.option_a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.option_b: Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
questions.option_c: A is true but R is false
questions.option_d: A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both true; temporal separation discourages selfing.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Assertion (A): Synergids guide pollen tube entry. Reason (R): Filiform apparatus is at micropylar tip of synergids. Choose the correct option:
questions.option_a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.option_b: Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
questions.option_c: A is true but R is false
questions.option_d: A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both true; R gives structural basis for guidance.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Regarding microsporangium wall in flowering plants (set 1), which statement is correct?
questions.option_a: It involves four layers as per NCERT
questions.option_c: It excludes any role in reproduction
questions.explanation: NCERT: microsporangium wall — epidermis, endothecium, middle layers, tapetum.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Regarding sporogenous tissue in flowering plants (set 2), which statement is correct?
questions.option_a: It involves occupies centre as per NCERT
questions.option_c: It excludes any role in reproduction
questions.explanation: NCERT: sporogenous tissue — gives rise to PMCs.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Regarding inflorescence in flowering plants (set 3), which statement is correct?
questions.option_a: It involves bears floral buds as per NCERT
questions.option_c: It excludes any role in reproduction
questions.explanation: NCERT: inflorescence — formed before flower opens.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Regarding gynoecium monocarpellary in flowering plants (set 4), which statement is correct?
questions.option_a: It involves single pistil as per NCERT
questions.option_c: It excludes any role in reproduction
questions.explanation: NCERT: gynoecium monocarpellary — vs multicarpellary.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Regarding stigma function in flowering plants (set 5), which statement is correct?
questions.option_a: It involves landing platform as per NCERT
questions.option_c: It excludes any role in reproduction
questions.explanation: NCERT: stigma function — for pollen grains.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Regarding style function in flowering plants (set 6), which statement is correct?
questions.option_a: It involves elongated slender part as per NCERT
questions.option_c: It excludes any role in reproduction
questions.explanation: NCERT: style function — connects stigma to ovary.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Regarding ovarian cavity in flowering plants (set 7), which statement is correct?
questions.option_a: It involves locule as per NCERT
questions.option_c: It excludes any role in reproduction
questions.explanation: NCERT: ovarian cavity — contains placenta and ovules.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Assertion (A): Double fertilisation produces zygote and primary endosperm nucleus. Reason (R): One sperm fuses with egg; other fuses with polar nuclei. Choose the correct option:
questions.option_a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.option_b: Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
questions.option_c: A is true but R is false
questions.option_d: A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Two fusion events: syngamy and triple fusion.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Humans reproduce by which mode and type of birth?
questions.explanation: Humans are sexually reproducing and give birth to live young (viviparous).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Blastocyst attachment to the uterine wall is termed:
questions.explanation: Attachment of the blastocyst to the uterine wall is called implantation.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Human reproductive events such as gametogenesis occur:
questions.explanation: Reproductive events in humans occur after attainment of puberty.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which statement about gamete formation in ageing humans is correct?
questions.option_a: Both sperm and ovum formation cease at age 50
questions.option_b: Sperm formation continues in old men while ovum formation ceases around age 50 in women
questions.option_c: Ovum formation continues lifelong in women
questions.option_d: Sperm formation ceases at puberty in males
questions.explanation: Spermatogenesis continues in old men, whereas oogenesis ceases around 50 years in women.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The male reproductive system is located in the:
questions.explanation: The male reproductive system is situated in the pelvis region.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The scrotum maintains testicular temperature approximately:
questions.option_c: 2-2.5°C lower than normal internal body temperature
questions.explanation: Scrotal temperature is 2-2.5°C below normal internal body temperature, essential for spermatogenesis.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Approximate adult dimensions of each testis are:
questions.explanation: Each adult testis is about 4-5 cm long and 2-3 cm wide.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Each testis contains approximately how many testicular lobules?
questions.explanation: Each testis has about 250 testicular lobules.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Each testicular lobule contains:
questions.explanation: Each lobule has one to three highly coiled seminiferous tubules where sperms are produced.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The inner lining of seminiferous tubules consists of:
questions.explanation: Seminiferous tubules are lined by spermatogonia (male germ cells) and Sertoli cells.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Sertoli cells in seminiferous tubules primarily:
questions.explanation: Sertoli cells nourish the dividing male germ cells.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Leydig cells are located in:
questions.explanation: Leydig (interstitial) cells lie in interstitial spaces outside seminiferous tubules.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Androgens are synthesised and secreted by:
questions.explanation: Leydig cells produce testicular androgens.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which is NOT a male sex accessory duct?
questions.explanation: Fallopian tubes are female accessory ducts; rete testis, vasa efferentia, epididymis and vas deferens are male.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Seminiferous tubules open into vasa efferentia via:
questions.explanation: Seminiferous tubules drain into rete testis, which connects to vasa efferentia.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Vasa efferentia open into the epididymis located on the:
questions.explanation: Vasa efferentia leave the testis and open into epididymis on the posterior testicular surface.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The vas deferens:
questions.option_a: Descends directly into urethra without looping
questions.option_b: Ascends to abdomen and loops over the urinary bladder
questions.explanation: Epididymis leads to vas deferens which ascends and loops over the urinary bladder.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The ejaculatory duct is formed by the union of vas deferens with a duct from the:
questions.explanation: Vas deferens receives a duct from the seminal vesicle and opens into urethra as ejaculatory duct.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Male accessory ducts primarily:
questions.option_b: Store and transport sperms to outside via urethra
questions.explanation: Accessory ducts store and transport sperms from testis to exterior through urethra.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The loose fold of skin covering the glans penis is the:
questions.explanation: Glans penis is covered by foreskin.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Male accessory glands include:
questions.option_a: Seminal vesicles, prostate and bulbourethral glands
questions.explanation: Male accessory glands are seminal vesicles, prostate and bulbourethral glands.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Seminal plasma is rich in:
questions.explanation: Seminal plasma contains fructose, calcium and enzymes from accessory gland secretions.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Bulbourethral gland secretions help in:
questions.explanation: Bulbourethral gland secretions lubricate the penis.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Ovarian stroma is divided into:
questions.explanation: Ovarian stroma has peripheral cortex and inner medulla.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Female accessory ducts include:
questions.explanation: Oviducts, uterus and vagina are female accessory ducts.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Each fallopian tube is approximately:
questions.explanation: Each fallopian tube is about 10-12 cm long.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Finger-like projections on the infundibulum that help collect the ovum are:
questions.explanation: Fimbriae on the infundibulum help collect the ovum after ovulation.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The wider part of the oviduct following the infundibulum is the:
questions.explanation: Infundibulum leads to the wider ampulla of the oviduct.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The narrow-lumen part of the oviduct joining the uterus is the:
questions.explanation: Isthmus is the narrow terminal part of the oviduct joining the uterus.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The uterus is also called the womb and is shaped like:
questions.explanation: The uterus (womb) is pear-shaped (inverted pear).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The uterus communicates with the vagina through the:
questions.explanation: Uterus opens into vagina via the narrow cervix.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The birth canal is formed by:
questions.explanation: Cervical canal plus vagina constitute the birth canal.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The inner glandular layer lining the uterine cavity is:
questions.explanation: Endometrium is the inner glandular layer of the uterus.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Strong uterine contractions during childbirth involve primarily the:
questions.explanation: Myometrium (middle smooth muscle layer) contracts strongly during delivery.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which is NOT part of female external genitalia?
questions.explanation: Cervix is internal; external genitalia include mons pubis, labia majora/minora, hymen and clitoris.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Labia majora:
questions.option_a: Extend from mons pubis and surround vaginal opening
questions.explanation: Labia majora are fleshy folds extending from mons pubis around the vaginal opening.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The vaginal opening is often partially covered by the:
questions.explanation: Hymen is a membrane that often partially covers the vaginal opening.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The clitoris lies:
questions.option_a: At upper junction of labia minora above urethral opening
questions.explanation: Clitoris is a small structure at the upper junction of labia minora above the urethral opening.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The hymen:
questions.option_a: Is a reliable indicator of virginity
questions.option_b: Is not a reliable indicator of virginity or sexual experience
questions.option_d: Is absent in all adult women
questions.explanation: Hymen presence or absence cannot reliably indicate virginity or sexual experience.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Each breast glandular tissue is divided into:
questions.explanation: Each breast has 15-20 mammary lobes containing alveoli.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Milk is expressed during breastfeeding from the:
questions.explanation: Milk flows through mammary ducts and lactiferous duct to the nipple.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Secondary spermatocytes contain:
questions.explanation: After meiosis I, secondary spermatocytes are haploid with 23 chromosomes each.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Meiosis II in spermatogenesis produces:
questions.explanation: Secondary spermatocytes undergo meiosis II to form four haploid spermatids.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Transformation of spermatids into spermatozoa is called:
questions.explanation: Spermatids become spermatozoa through spermiogenesis.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: GnRH stimulates the anterior pituitary to secrete:
questions.explanation: GnRH stimulates LH and FSH secretion from anterior pituitary.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: LH stimulates spermatogenesis indirectly by acting on:
questions.explanation: LH acts on Leydig cells; androgens then stimulate spermatogenesis.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: FSH in males acts primarily on:
questions.explanation: FSH acts on Sertoli cells, aiding spermiogenesis.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The cap-like structure on the anterior sperm head is the:
questions.explanation: Acrosome is a cap-like structure covering the anterior sperm head.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Acrosomal enzymes help in:
questions.explanation: Acrosome enzymes facilitate fertilisation.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Mitochondria in the sperm middle piece provide energy for:
questions.explanation: Middle-piece mitochondria power tail motility needed for fertilisation.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: For normal human male fertility, at least what percentage of ejaculated sperms must show vigorous motility?
questions.explanation: At least 40% of sperms must show vigorous motility for normal fertility.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Sperm maturation and motility depend on secretions from:
questions.option_a: Epididymis, vas deferens, seminal vesicle and prostate
questions.explanation: Accessory duct and gland secretions are essential for sperm maturation and motility.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Male accessory ducts and glands are maintained by:
questions.explanation: Testicular androgens maintain accessory duct and gland functions.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Oogonia are formed during embryonic development and:
questions.option_a: No more oogonia are added after birth
questions.explanation: Oogonia form in fetal ovary; no new oogonia are added after birth.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Primary oocytes are oogonia arrested at:
questions.explanation: Oogonia enter prophase-I and arrest as primary oocytes.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: At puberty, approximately how many primary follicles remain in each ovary?
questions.explanation: Only 60,000-80,000 primary follicles remain per ovary at puberty.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The fluid-filled cavity in a tertiary follicle is the:
questions.explanation: Tertiary follicles have a fluid-filled antrum.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The theca layer of developing follicles has:
questions.explanation: Theca is organised into inner theca interna and outer theca externa.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: First meiotic division of primary oocyte produces:
questions.option_a: Secondary oocyte and first polar body
questions.explanation: Unequal meiosis I yields a large secondary oocyte and tiny first polar body.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The secondary oocyte retains:
questions.option_a: Most nutrient-rich cytoplasm of the primary oocyte
questions.explanation: Secondary oocyte retains bulk of nutrient-rich cytoplasm.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: A mature ovarian follicle ready for ovulation is the:
questions.explanation: Tertiary follicle matures into Graafian follicle.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The membrane surrounding the secondary oocyte is:
questions.explanation: Secondary oocyte is surrounded by zona pellucida.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Release of secondary oocyte from ovary is called:
questions.explanation: Rupture of Graafian follicle releasing oocyte is ovulation.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The first menstruation at puberty is termed:
questions.explanation: First menstruation at puberty is menarche.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Average interval between menstrual cycles in human females is about:
questions.explanation: Menstrual cycle repeats at average interval of about 28-29 days.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Menstrual flow results from breakdown of:
questions.option_a: Endometrial lining and its blood vessels
questions.explanation: Breakdown of endometrium and blood vessels produces menstrual flow.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: During the follicular phase:
questions.option_a: Primary follicles mature and endometrium regenerates
questions.explanation: Follicular phase involves follicle growth and endometrial proliferation.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: During follicular phase, increasing LH and FSH stimulate:
questions.explanation: Rising LH/FSH promote follicle growth and estrogen secretion.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: LH and FSH peak occurs around:
questions.explanation: LH and FSH peak around the 14th day (mid-cycle).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Ovulation is induced by:
questions.explanation: Mid-cycle LH surge triggers Graafian follicle rupture and ovulation.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: After ovulation, the remaining follicle becomes the:
questions.explanation: Post-ovulation luteal phase forms corpus luteum from follicle remnants.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Corpus luteum primarily secretes:
questions.explanation: Corpus luteum secretes progesterone to maintain endometrium.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Progesterone-maintained endometrium is necessary for:
questions.explanation: Progesterone-prepared endometrium supports implantation and pregnancy.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: During pregnancy:
questions.option_a: Menstrual cycle events cease and menstruation stops
questions.explanation: Pregnancy halts the menstrual cycle and menstruation.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: If fertilisation does not occur:
questions.option_a: Corpus luteum degenerates and menstruation begins a new cycle
questions.explanation: Without fertilisation, corpus luteum degenerates, endometrium breaks down, and a new cycle starts.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Cessation of menstrual cycles around age 50 is called:
questions.explanation: Menopause is cessation of menstrual cycles around 50 years.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Cyclic menstruation indicates normal reproductive phase between:
questions.explanation: Regular menstruation marks the fertile period from menarche to menopause.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Sperms reach the site of fertilisation in the:
questions.explanation: Motile sperms travel to the ampulla of the fallopian tube.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Fertilisation normally occurs in the:
questions.explanation: Ovum and sperm meet in the ampullary region.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Not all copulations result in pregnancy because:
questions.option_a: Ovum and sperms must reach ampulla simultaneously
questions.option_c: Only one sperm is ever produced
questions.explanation: Simultaneous transport of gametes to ampulla is required for fertilisation.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Contact with zona pellucida during fertilisation ensures:
questions.option_a: Only one sperm fertilises the ovum
questions.explanation: Zona pellucida changes block polyspermy, allowing one sperm to fertilise.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Acrosome secretions help sperm:
questions.option_a: Penetrate zona pellucida and enter ovum cytoplasm
questions.explanation: Acrosomal enzymes help sperm penetrate zona pellucida and plasma membrane.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Fertilisation triggers completion of meiosis II in secondary oocyte, producing:
questions.explanation: Meiosis II yields haploid ootid and second polar body.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Approximately what percentage of human sperms carry Y chromosome?
questions.explanation: About 50% of sperms carry X and 50% carry Y.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: A zygote with XY chromosomes will develop into a:
questions.explanation: XY zygote develops into male; XX into female.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Sex of the human baby is determined by:
questions.explanation: Father contributes X or Y sperm; mother always contributes X.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Morula transforms into blastocyst as it moves into the:
questions.explanation: Morula becomes blastocyst while moving into uterus.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Blastocyst consists of:
questions.explanation: Blastocyst has outer trophoblast and inner cell mass.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: In blastocyst, the inner cell mass differentiates into the:
questions.explanation: Inner cell mass forms the embryo; trophoblast attaches to endometrium.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Finger-like projections on trophoblast after implantation are:
questions.explanation: Chorionic villi are finger-like trophoblast projections.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The placenta is formed by interdigitation of:
questions.explanation: Placenta forms from chorionic villi and uterine tissue interdigitation.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Functions of placenta include:
questions.explanation: Placenta exchanges O2, nutrients, CO2 and wastes between mother and embryo.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: hCG, hPL and relaxin are produced:
questions.explanation: These hormones are pregnancy-specific in women.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Elevated pregnancy hormones support:
questions.option_a: Fetal growth, maternal metabolic changes and pregnancy maintenance
questions.explanation: High hormone levels support fetal growth and maternal pregnancy physiology.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: All adult tissues and organs arise from:
questions.explanation: Three germ layers give rise to all adult tissues and organs.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Stem cells in inner cell mass can:
questions.option_a: Give rise to all tissues and organs
questions.explanation: Inner cell mass stem cells are pluripotent for all tissues/organs.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: After one month of pregnancy, the embryo's ___ is formed.
questions.explanation: Embryonic heart forms after about one month.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: By end of second month of pregnancy, foetus develops:
questions.explanation: Limbs and digits appear by end of second month.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: By end of 12 weeks (first trimester):
questions.option_a: Most major organ systems including limbs and external genitalia are formed
questions.explanation: First trimester ends with most major organs including external genitalia formed.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: First foetal movements and head hair usually appear in:
questions.explanation: Fifth month typically shows first movements and head hair.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: By 24 weeks (end of second trimester):
questions.option_a: Fine body hair, separated eyelids and eyelashes are present
questions.explanation: At 24 weeks, fine hair, separated eyelids and eyelashes form.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: At nine months of pregnancy the foetus is:
questions.option_a: Fully developed and ready for delivery
questions.explanation: Nine-month foetus is fully developed and ready for birth.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The gestation period in humans is about:
questions.explanation: Human gestation averages about nine months.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Foetal ejection reflex is triggered by signals from:
questions.explanation: Foetus and placenta initiate foetal ejection reflex.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: During parturition, oxytocin causes:
questions.option_a: Stronger uterine contractions in a positive feedback loop
questions.explanation: Oxytocin strengthens contractions, stimulating more oxytocin release.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The baby is expelled through the:
questions.explanation: Baby is expelled via birth canal during parturition.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: After infant delivery:
questions.explanation: Placenta is expelled shortly after the baby.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Colostrum is important because it:
questions.option_a: Contains antibodies essential for newborn resistance
questions.explanation: Colostrum provides antibodies critical for newborn immunity.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Scrotum location of testes is essential because spermatogenesis requires:
questions.explanation: Low scrotal temperature is necessary for sperm formation.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Testosterone is synthesised by:
questions.explanation: Leydig cells in interstitial spaces produce androgens.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Seminiferous tubules open into vasa efferentia through:
questions.explanation: Rete testis is network connecting tubules to vasa efferentia.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Fructose-rich seminal plasma is contributed mainly by:
questions.option_b: Seminal vesicles and other accessory glands
questions.explanation: Accessory gland secretions form seminal plasma rich in fructose and enzymes.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Gamete-producing region of ovary is primarily the:
questions.explanation: Cortex contains follicles; medulla has blood vessels and nerves.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Finger-like fimbriae of fallopian tube help in:
questions.explanation: Fimbriae sweep ovum into infundibulum.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Fertilisation in humans normally occurs in:
questions.explanation: Sperm and ovum meet in ampulla of oviduct.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Strong uterine contractions during delivery involve:
questions.explanation: Myometrium (smooth muscle) contracts vigorously during parturition.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which statement about hymen is correct?
questions.option_b: It may persist after coitus or tear without intercourse
questions.option_c: It is absent in all adult females
questions.explanation: Hymen can break from tampons, sports, or persist after coitus—unreliable indicator.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Haploid spermatids are formed after:
questions.option_b: Two meiotic divisions of primary spermatocyte
questions.explanation: Primary spermatocyte completes meiosis I and II producing four spermatids.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Increased GnRH at puberty acts on:
questions.option_b: Anterior pituitary to release LH and FSH
questions.explanation: Hypothalamic GnRH stimulates gonadotropin secretion.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: FSH in males primarily acts on:
questions.explanation: FSH stimulates Sertoli cells; LH stimulates Leydig/androgens.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Acrosome of sperm contains:
questions.explanation: Acrosome cap has enzymes for fertilisation.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Primary oocytes are arrested at:
questions.option_b: Prophase I of meiosis from fetal life
questions.explanation: Oogonia enter prophase I prenatally and remain arrested until ovulation.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Tertiary follicle stage completes first meiosis producing:
questions.option_a: Equal-sized secondary oocyte and polar body
questions.option_b: Large secondary oocyte and tiny first polar body
questions.explanation: Unequal division retains cytoplasm in secondary oocyte.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Ovulation releases:
questions.option_a: Primary oocyte arrested at prophase I
questions.explanation: Graafian follicle releases secondary oocyte; meiosis II completes after fertilisation.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Menstrual phase of cycle is characterised by:
questions.explanation: Days 3-5: menstrual flow from endometrial breakdown.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Rising estrogen during follicular phase comes from:
questions.explanation: Growing follicles secrete estrogens during follicular phase.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Ovulation is triggered by:
questions.explanation: Rapid LH secretion (LH surge) induces Graafian follicle rupture.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: After ovulation, progesterone mainly comes from:
questions.explanation: Corpus luteum maintains endometrium via progesterone.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Menstruation begins when:
questions.option_b: Corpus luteum degenerates and endometrium breaks down
questions.explanation: CL regression lowers progesterone → endometrial shedding.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Cessation of menstrual cycle around 50 years is called:
questions.explanation: Menopause marks end of reproductive phase.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Entry of first sperm induces changes preventing:
questions.explanation: Membrane block ensures monospermy.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Second polar body forms during:
questions.option_b: Completion of meiosis II after fertilisation
questions.explanation: Sperm entry triggers completion of meiosis II in oocyte.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Human zygote with XY complement develops into:
questions.explanation: Sperm carries X or Y; XX = female, XY = male.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Trophoblast of blastocyst forms:
questions.explanation: Trophoblast attaches to endometrium and forms chorionic villi.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Implantation refers to:
questions.explanation: Blastocyst becomes embedded in uterine lining.

questions.question: hCG is secreted by:

questions.question: Reproductive health, in its broader sense, includes:
questions.option_a: Only the physical condition of reproductive organs
questions.option_b: Healthy reproductive organs along with emotional and social aspects of reproduction
questions.explanation: Reproductive health covers normal organ function as well as emotional and social dimensions of reproduction.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: According to WHO, reproductive health means total well-being in which aspects of reproduction?
questions.explanation: WHO defines reproductive health as complete well-being across physical, emotional, behavioural and social aspects.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: India's initiative to attain reproductive health as a social goal at the national level was:
questions.option_a: One of the last among developing nations
questions.option_b: Among the first countries in the world to do so
questions.explanation: India was among the earliest nations to launch national-level reproductive health programmes.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Family planning programmes in India were initiated in:
questions.explanation: India began its family planning programmes in 1951.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The current improved reproduction-related programmes in India are known as:
questions.option_b: Reproductive and Child Health Care (RCH) programmes
questions.explanation: RCH programmes are the current name for wider reproduction-related health programmes in India.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The major tasks under reproductive health programmes include:
questions.option_b: Creating awareness and providing facilities for a reproductively healthy society
questions.option_d: Restricting medical care to urban areas only
questions.explanation: RCH programmes focus on awareness creation and infrastructural support for reproductive health.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Sex education in schools is encouraged primarily to:
questions.option_b: Provide correct information and discourage myths and misconceptions about sex-related aspects
questions.explanation: School sex education aims to give accurate information and counter myths among adolescents.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Information about reproductive organs, adolescence, safe sexual practices and STDs/AIDS especially benefits:
questions.option_b: People, especially those in the adolescent age group
questions.explanation: Adolescents particularly benefit from proper reproductive and sexual health information.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Educating fertile couples and those in the marriageable age group should include all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.option_a: Birth control options and care of pregnant mothers
questions.option_b: Post-natal care and importance of breast feeding
questions.option_c: Equal opportunities for male and female children
questions.option_d: Encouraging indiscriminate use of amniocentesis for sex selection
questions.explanation: Reproductive health education promotes family planning and maternal-child care, not sex-selective practices.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Successful implementation of reproductive health action plans requires:
questions.option_b: Strong infrastructural facilities, professional expertise and material support
questions.option_d: Restriction of services to private clinics
questions.explanation: Infrastructure, trained professionals and material resources are essential for reproductive health programmes.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Reproductive health facilities provide medical assistance for all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Reproductive health care covers pregnancy, delivery, STDs, MTP, contraception, menstrual and infertility issues.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Amniocentesis for sex-determination is banned in India to:
questions.option_b: Legally check the increasing menace of female foeticides
questions.option_d: Encourage early detection of all genetic disorders
questions.explanation: The statutory ban on amniocentesis for sex determination aims to prevent female foeticide.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: In amniocentesis, which material is sampled for analysis?
questions.option_b: Amniotic fluid of the developing foetus
questions.explanation: Amniocentesis involves sampling amniotic fluid to analyse fetal cells and dissolved substances.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Amniocentesis is legitimately used to detect:
questions.option_a: Only the sex of the foetus
questions.option_b: Genetic disorders such as Down syndrome, haemophilia and sickle-cell anaemia
questions.explanation: Amniocentesis can detect genetic disorders and assess fetal survivability, not for sex selection.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The oral contraceptive 'Saheli' was developed at:
questions.explanation: Saheli was developed by scientists at CDRI in Lucknow, India.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which of the following indicates improved reproductive health in society?
questions.option_a: Increased maternal and infant mortality rates
questions.option_b: Decreased maternal and infant mortality rates and better detection of STDs
questions.explanation: Reduced maternal/infant mortality and better STD management are indicators of improved reproductive health.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The world population in 2011 was approximately:
questions.explanation: World population grew from about 2 billion in 1900 to 7.2 billion by 2011.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: India's population at the time of independence was approximately:
questions.explanation: India had about 350 million people at independence and crossed 1.2 billion by May 2011.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Probable reasons for population explosion in India include:
questions.option_a: Increase in death rate and IMR
questions.option_b: Rapid decline in death rate, MMR and IMR along with more people in reproductive age
questions.option_c: Decrease in people of reproductive age
questions.explanation: Lower mortality rates and a larger reproductive-age population contributed to population growth.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: According to the 2011 census, India's population growth rate was:
questions.option_a: Less than 2 per cent (20 per 1000 per year)
questions.option_d: More than 10 per cent per year
questions.explanation: The 2011 census reported a growth rate below 2%, still high enough for rapid population increase.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: An ideal contraceptive should be:
questions.option_b: User-friendly, effective, reversible with minimal side effects and no interference with sexual drive
questions.option_c: Effective only by suppressing sexual desire
questions.explanation: Ideal contraceptives are accessible, effective, reversible, safe and do not affect normal sexual function.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a broad category of contraceptive methods mentioned in NCERT?
questions.explanation: NCERT groups contraceptives into natural, barrier, IUDs, oral, injectables, implants and surgical methods.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The statutory marriageable ages in India are:
questions.explanation: The legal marriageable age is 18 years for females and 21 years for males in India.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Natural contraceptive methods work on the principle of:
questions.option_b: Avoiding chances of ovum and sperm meeting
questions.explanation: Natural methods prevent fertilisation by avoiding contact between ovum and sperm.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: In periodic abstinence, couples avoid coitus during:
questions.option_a: Days 1 to 5 of the menstrual cycle
questions.option_b: Days 10 to 17 of the menstrual cycle
questions.explanation: Days 10–17 represent the fertile period when ovulation is expected.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Coitus interruptus involves:
questions.option_b: Male partner withdrawing the penis just before ejaculation
questions.option_c: Administration of oral pills after intercourse
questions.explanation: Coitus interruptus relies on withdrawal before ejaculation to prevent insemination.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Lactational amenorrhea method is based on:
questions.option_a: Ovulation occurring more frequently during lactation
questions.option_b: Absence of ovulation and menstrual cycle during intense lactation after parturition
questions.option_c: Use of copper ions in the uterus
questions.explanation: Intense breastfeeding after childbirth suppresses ovulation and menstruation.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The lactational amenorrhea method is effective for a maximum of:
questions.explanation: Lactational amenorrhea is considered effective only up to six months postpartum.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Natural contraceptive methods are characterised by:
questions.option_a: High side effects and low failure rates
questions.option_b: Almost nil side effects but high chances of failure
questions.explanation: Natural methods have minimal side effects but relatively high failure rates.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Condoms prevent conception by:
questions.option_b: Covering the penis or vagina and cervix to prevent semen entering the female tract
questions.option_c: Releasing copper ions in the uterus
questions.explanation: Condoms are physical barriers that keep ejaculated semen out of the female reproductive tract.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: 'Nirodh' is a popular brand of:
questions.explanation: Nirodh is a well-known brand of male condoms in India.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Apart from contraception, condoms also help in:
questions.explanation: Condoms provide a barrier against sexually transmitted infections including HIV/AIDS.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Male and female condoms are:
questions.option_b: Disposable and can be self-inserted, offering privacy
questions.explanation: Condoms are disposable barrier devices that users can apply themselves.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Diaphragms, cervical caps and vaults:
questions.option_a: Are inserted into the uterus permanently
questions.option_b: Are rubber barriers inserted to cover the cervix during coitus
questions.explanation: These reusable rubber barriers cover the cervix to block sperm entry.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Spermicidal creams, jellies and foams are used with barrier methods to:
questions.explanation: Spermicides enhance the effectiveness of barrier contraceptives.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which of the following is a copper-releasing IUD?
questions.explanation: CuT, Cu7 and Multiload 375 are copper-releasing IUDs; Lippes loop is non-medicated.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Copper-releasing IUDs prevent pregnancy by:
questions.option_b: Increasing phagocytosis of sperms and suppressing sperm motility and fertilising capacity
questions.explanation: IUDs promote sperm phagocytosis and copper ions impair sperm motility and fertilisation.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Hormone-releasing IUDs additionally:
questions.option_b: Make the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to sperms
questions.option_d: Replace the need for condoms against HIV
questions.explanation: Hormonal IUDs alter the uterine and cervical environment to prevent fertilisation and implantation.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: IUDs are especially suitable for women who wish to:
questions.explanation: IUDs are widely used in India for spacing and delaying pregnancies.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Oral contraceptive pills are taken:
questions.option_b: Daily for 21 days, followed by a 7-day gap, then repeated
questions.option_c: Only on the day of ovulation
questions.option_d: Once a month without any gap
questions.explanation: The pill regimen is 21 active days, 7-day break (menstruation), then repeat.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Oral contraceptive pills act by:
questions.option_b: Inhibiting ovulation and implantation and altering cervical mucus
questions.explanation: Pills suppress ovulation and implantation and thicken cervical mucus to block sperm.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Saheli oral contraceptive is distinctive because it is:
questions.option_b: A once-a-week non-steroidal pill with few side effects
questions.explanation: Saheli is a weekly non-steroidal oral contraceptive developed in India.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Injectable and implant contraceptives differ from pills mainly in having:
questions.option_b: Similar mode of action but much longer effective periods
questions.explanation: Injectables and implants work like pills but provide contraception for longer durations.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Emergency contraceptives are most effective when administered within:
questions.explanation: Progestogen combinations or IUDs within 72 hours of intercourse serve as emergency contraception.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Surgical contraceptive methods are also called:
questions.explanation: Surgical methods permanently block gamete transport and are termed sterilisation.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Sterilisation in the male and female is called respectively:
questions.explanation: Vasectomy is male sterilisation; tubectomy is female sterilisation.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Vasectomy involves:
questions.option_a: Removal or tying of a part of the fallopian tube
questions.option_b: Removal or tying of a part of the vas deferens through a scrotal incision
questions.option_d: Injection of sclerosing agents into the uterus
questions.explanation: Vasectomy blocks sperm transport by cutting or ligating the vas deferens.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Surgical sterilisation methods are:
questions.option_b: Highly effective with very poor reversibility
questions.explanation: Vasectomy and tubectomy are very effective but difficult to reverse.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The MTP (Amendment) Act, 2017 was enacted to:
questions.option_b: Reduce illegal abortions and consequent maternal mortality and morbidity
questions.option_d: Allow abortion only after 24 weeks without conditions
questions.explanation: The 2017 amendment aimed to curb unsafe illegal abortions and protect maternal health.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Under the MTP (Amendment) Act, 2017, termination within the first 12 weeks requires the opinion of:
questions.explanation: Termination up to 12 weeks needs approval from one registered medical practitioner.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: For MTP between 12 and 24 weeks of pregnancy, the opinion of how many registered medical practitioners is required?
questions.explanation: Between 12 and 24 weeks, two registered practitioners must agree in good faith.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Grounds for legal termination of pregnancy under the MTP Act include:
questions.option_b: Risk to the woman's life or grave injury to her health, or substantial risk of serious fetal handicap
questions.option_c: Economic inconvenience alone without health risk
questions.explanation: Legal grounds include maternal health risk and risk of serious fetal abnormalities.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Selection of a suitable contraceptive method should:
questions.option_b: Always be undertaken in consultation with qualified medical professionals
questions.explanation: Medical guidance ensures safe and appropriate contraceptive choice.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Contraceptives are:
questions.option_a: Regular requirements for maintaining reproductive health
questions.option_b: Not regular requirements for the maintenance of reproductive health
questions.explanation: Contraceptives are used to prevent or space pregnancy, not as routine reproductive health maintenance.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Possible side effects of contraceptives mentioned in NCERT include:
questions.option_b: Nausea, abdominal pain, breakthrough bleeding and irregular menstrual bleeding
questions.option_c: Complete loss of sexual desire in all users
questions.option_d: Guaranteed protection against all STIs when using pills alone
questions.explanation: Contraceptives may cause nausea, pain, breakthrough bleeding and other effects that warrant attention.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Medical termination of pregnancy (MTP) is:
questions.option_a: Spontaneous loss of pregnancy at full term
questions.option_b: Intentional or voluntary termination of pregnancy before full term
questions.explanation: MTP refers to deliberate termination of pregnancy before full term, also called induced abortion.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Approximately what fraction of conceived pregnancies worldwide result in MTPs annually?
questions.explanation: About 45–50 million MTPs per year represent roughly one-fifth of all conceived pregnancies.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: MTP was legalised in India in:
questions.explanation: India legalised MTP in 1971 under strict conditions to prevent misuse.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: MTPs are considered relatively safe during:
questions.explanation: First-trimester MTPs (up to 12 weeks) are relatively safe; later abortions carry higher risk.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: A major concern regarding MTPs in India is that:
questions.option_a: All MTPs are performed only in government hospitals
questions.option_b: A majority are performed illegally by unqualified persons and can be fatal
questions.explanation: Many illegal MTPs by unqualified practitioners pose serious health risks.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Misuse of amniocentesis followed by MTP when the fetus is female is:
questions.explanation: Using amniocentesis for sex selection followed by female feticide is illegal.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Infections transmitted through sexual intercourse are collectively called:
questions.option_b: STIs, venereal diseases (VD) or reproductive tract infections (RTI)
questions.explanation: STIs/VDs/RTIs are infections spread primarily through sexual contact.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed as a common STI in NCERT Chapter 3?
questions.explanation: NCERT lists gonorrhoea, syphilis, herpes, chlamydia, warts, trichomoniasis, hepatitis-B and HIV as STIs.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Among common STIs, which infection is described as the most dangerous?
questions.explanation: HIV/AIDS is considered the most dangerous STI and is covered in detail in Chapter 7.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Hepatitis-B and HIV can spread through all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.option_a: Sharing injection needles with infected persons
questions.option_c: Transmission from infected mother to foetus
questions.explanation: Hepatitis-B and HIV spread via needles, blood products and mother-to-child transmission, not casual contact.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which STIs are NOT completely curable even with early detection?
questions.option_d: Genital warts only among all listed
questions.explanation: Hepatitis-B, genital herpes and HIV cannot be completely cured; most other STIs are curable if treated early.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Early symptoms of most STIs include:
questions.option_b: Itching, fluid discharge, slight pain and swellings in the genital region
questions.option_c: Complete absence of any signs always
questions.option_d: High fever and rash all over the body in every case
questions.explanation: Early STI symptoms are often mild local signs in the genital area.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Infected females with STIs:
questions.option_b: May often be asymptomatic and remain undetected for long
questions.explanation: Many infected women show few or no symptoms, delaying diagnosis and treatment.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Untreated STIs may lead to complications such as:
questions.option_b: PID, still births, ectopic pregnancies, infertility and reproductive tract cancer
questions.explanation: Late complications of STIs include PID, pregnancy losses, ectopic pregnancy, infertility and cancer.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: STI incidence is reported to be very high among persons in the age group of:
questions.explanation: Adolescents and young adults (15–24 years) show particularly high STI incidence.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Precautions to avoid STIs include:
questions.option_a: Having multiple unknown partners without protection
questions.option_b: Avoiding unknown/multiple partners, using condoms and seeking early medical care
questions.explanation: STI prevention involves partner caution, condom use and prompt qualified medical care.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Infertility refers to couples who:
questions.option_b: Are unable to produce children despite unprotected sexual cohabitation
questions.explanation: Infertile couples cannot conceive despite unprotected regular sexual cohabitation.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: According to the chapter summary, infertility is defined as inability to conceive after:
questions.explanation: The summary defines infertility as failure to conceive after two years of unprotected cohabitation.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Causes of infertility may include:
questions.option_b: Physical, congenital, diseases, drugs, immunological and psychological factors
questions.option_d: Excessive exercise alone in all cases
questions.explanation: Infertility has diverse causes including physical, congenital, disease, drug, immune and psychological factors.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Regarding infertility in India, NCERT states that:
questions.option_a: The problem always lies in the female partner
questions.option_b: Females are often blamed but the problem frequently lies in the male partner
questions.option_c: Males are never responsible for infertility
questions.explanation: Although women are often blamed, male factors are frequently responsible for infertility.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: When corrective treatment for infertility is not possible, couples may be helped through:
questions.explanation: ART techniques assist infertile couples when conventional treatment cannot restore fertility.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The 'test tube baby' programme involves:
questions.option_a: Fertilisation inside the fallopian tube only
questions.option_b: IVF (fertilisation outside the body) followed by embryo transfer
questions.option_d: Only artificial insemination into the vagina
questions.explanation: Test tube baby programmes use IVF in the laboratory followed by transfer of the embryo.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: ZIFT involves transfer of:
questions.option_a: Embryos with more than 8 blastomeres into the uterus
questions.option_b: Zygote or early embryos with up to 8 blastomeres into the fallopian tube
questions.option_d: A donor ovum into the uterus without fertilisation
questions.explanation: ZIFT places zygotes or early embryos (up to 8 blastomeres) into the fallopian tube.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: GIFT (gamete intra fallopian transfer) involves:
questions.option_a: Transfer of a donor ovum into the fallopian tube of a recipient female
questions.option_b: Injection of sperm directly into the ovum in the lab
questions.option_c: Surgical removal of the vas deferens
questions.option_d: Transfer of embryo with more than 8 blastomeres only
questions.explanation: GIFT transfers a donor ovum into the recipient's fallopian tube for in vivo fertilisation.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: ICSI is a procedure in which:
questions.option_a: Multiple sperms are placed in the fallopian tube
questions.option_b: A sperm is directly injected into the ovum in the laboratory
questions.option_c: An IUD is inserted into the uterus
questions.option_d: An ovum is transferred without any sperm
questions.explanation: ICSI involves direct microinjection of a single sperm into an ovum to form an embryo.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Artificial insemination (AI) is useful when:
questions.option_b: The male cannot inseminate the female or has very low sperm count
questions.explanation: AI introduces semen from the husband or donor into the vagina or uterus (IUI) to overcome male fertility issues.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: ART facilities in India are limited because they:
questions.option_b: Require high precision, specialised professionals and expensive equipment
questions.option_d: Are available at every primary health centre
questions.explanation: ART demands skilled personnel and costly equipment, so centres offering these services are few.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Apart from ART, NCERT suggests that couples seeking parenthood may consider:
questions.option_b: Legal adoption permitted under Indian law
questions.explanation: Legal adoption is presented as a meaningful option for couples desiring children.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Governmental and non-governmental agencies create reproductive health awareness using:
questions.explanation: Agencies use audio-visual and print media to spread reproduction-related information.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Who among the following has a major role in disseminating reproductive health information?
questions.explanation: Family members, teachers and peers play an important role in reproductive health education.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Reproductive health awareness should also address:
questions.option_b: Uncontrolled population growth and social evils like sex-abuse and sex-related crimes
questions.explanation: Awareness programmes also target population issues and sex-related social problems.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The most important step to overcome population explosion is to:
questions.option_b: Motivate smaller families using various contraceptive methods
questions.explanation: Promoting smaller families through contraception is key to addressing population growth.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The family planning slogan 'Hum Do Hamare Do' means:
questions.explanation: Hum Do Hamare Do promotes a family of two children for the couple.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: IUDs are inserted into the uterus:
questions.option_a: By the user without any training
questions.option_b: By doctors or expert nurses through the vagina
questions.option_c: Through an abdominal incision only in all cases
questions.explanation: Trained medical personnel insert IUDs through the vagina into the uterus.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: MTP may be sought to terminate pregnancies resulting from:
questions.option_b: Casual unprotected intercourse, contraceptive failure or rape
questions.explanation: MTP addresses unwanted pregnancies from unprotected sex, contraceptive failure or sexual assault.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: MTP may also be essential when:
questions.option_a: The couple wants a male child only
questions.option_b: Continuation of pregnancy could be harmful or fatal to the mother, foetus or both
questions.option_c: The pregnancy is wanted and healthy
questions.explanation: MTP is medically indicated when continuing pregnancy endangers the mother or fetus.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: To reverse unhealthy trends in MTP practices, NCERT recommends:
questions.option_b: Counselling against unprotected coitus, warning about illegal abortions and expanding health care facilities
questions.explanation: Counselling and better health facilities can reduce unsafe and illegal abortion practices.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Delayed treatment of STIs is often due to:
questions.option_a: Immediate severe symptoms in all cases
questions.option_b: Mild early symptoms and social stigma
questions.option_d: Free universal treatment at all villages
questions.explanation: Mild symptoms and stigma prevent people from seeking timely STI diagnosis and treatment.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Infertility clinics help couples by:
questions.option_b: Diagnosing and correcting some reproductive disorders
questions.explanation: Infertility clinics diagnose disorders and offer corrective treatments to help conception.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Embryos formed by in-vivo fertilisation can be used to:
questions.option_a: Determine the sex of the child legally
questions.option_b: Assist females who cannot conceive through embryo transfer
questions.option_c: Replace the need for all contraceptive methods
questions.explanation: Embryos from in-vivo fertilisation may be transferred to help women who cannot conceive naturally.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The RCH programme's effect on population growth rate has been:
questions.option_a: A complete halt of population growth
questions.explanation: RCH programmes reduced growth rate only marginally despite improvements in health.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: An alarming population growth rate may lead to scarcity of:
questions.option_b: Basic requirements like food, shelter and clothing
questions.explanation: Rapid population growth can outpace resources for food, shelter and clothing.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Surgical contraceptive methods prevent conception by:
questions.option_a: Preventing gamete formation in the gonads
questions.option_c: Destroying the zygote after implantation only
questions.explanation: Vasectomy and tubectomy block transport of gametes rather than stopping their formation.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Under reproductive health-care programmes, STIs receive priority emphasis on:
questions.explanation: RCH programmes prioritise STI prevention and early diagnosis and treatment.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Adoption of ART methods may be limited by:
questions.option_b: Emotional, religious and social factors in addition to cost and availability
questions.explanation: Beyond technical and financial barriers, emotional, religious and social attitudes affect ART adoption.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Reproductive health according to WHO includes:
questions.option_b: Physical, emotional, behavioural and social well-being
questions.explanation: WHO definition covers all aspects of reproductive well-being.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: India's national family planning programme began in:
questions.explanation: India was among first countries with national action plans from 1951.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Saheli contraceptive developed in India is:
questions.explanation: Saheli from CDRI Lucknow—non-steroidal weekly pill.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Fertile period for periodic abstinence is approximately:
questions.explanation: Ovulation window—abstinence during days 10-17.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Lactational amenorrhea method is effective for about:
questions.explanation: Intense lactation suppresses ovulation up to ~6 months.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Major additional benefit of condom use is:
questions.explanation: Barrier prevents pathogen transmission.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Copper releasing IUDs prevent pregnancy partly by:
questions.option_b: Cu ions reducing sperm motility and fertilising capacity
questions.explanation: Cu ions suppress sperm function; also increase phagocytosis.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Combined oral contraceptive pill regimen is:
questions.explanation: 21 active days + 7 gap when menstruation occurs.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Post-coital emergency contraception is effective if used within:
questions.explanation: Progestogen/IUD within 72 hours of unprotected intercourse.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Tubectomy in females involves:
questions.explanation: Tubectomy blocks oviduct; vasectomy blocks vas deferens.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: MTP Act 1971 aims to reduce:
questions.explanation: Legal MTP reduces unsafe illegal abortion deaths.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: MTP is considered relatively safe during:
questions.explanation: First trimester MTP safer; second trimester riskier.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Statutory ban on amniocentesis for sex determination prevents:
questions.explanation: Misuse for sex-selective MTP is illegal.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: STI that can also spread via shared needles includes:
questions.explanation: HIV and HBV spread by blood/needle sharing too.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Why STIs often remain undetected in females?
questions.option_b: Mild/absent early symptoms and social stigma
questions.explanation: Asymptomatic early stages + stigma delay treatment.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Test tube baby programme involves:
questions.explanation: Ova and sperm fertilised in vitro; embryo transferred.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: ZIFT differs from IUT because ZIFT transfers:
questions.explanation: Zygote intra-fallopian transfer vs intra-uterine transfer.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: In GIFT procedure:
questions.option_b: Donor ovum transferred to fallopian tube of recipient
questions.explanation: Gamete intra-fallopian transfer—ovum into tube for in vivo fertilisation.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: ICSI technique involves:
questions.option_a: Mixing many sperm with ova in dish only
questions.option_b: Direct injection of sperm into ovum cytoplasm
questions.explanation: Intra-cytoplasmic sperm injection for severe male factor infertility.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Intra-uterine insemination (IUI) is:
questions.option_b: Artificial introduction of semen into uterus
questions.explanation: AI/IUI bypasses low sperm count or insemination failure.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Assertion (A): Condoms prevent pregnancy. Reason (R): They also reduce STI/HIV transmission. Choose the correct option:
questions.option_a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.option_b: Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
questions.option_c: A is true but R is false
questions.option_d: A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both true; R adds STI protection benefit.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Assertion (A): CuT is contraceptive IUD. Reason (R): Copper ions suppress sperm motility. Choose the correct option:
questions.option_a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.option_b: Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
questions.option_c: A is true but R is false
questions.option_d: A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both true; R explains part of mechanism.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Assertion (A): First trimester MTP is relatively safe. Reason (R): Second trimester abortions are riskier. Choose the correct option:
questions.option_a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.option_b: Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
questions.option_c: A is true but R is false
questions.option_d: A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both true; R contrasts trimester risk.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Assertion (A): IVF is fertilisation outside body. Reason (R): Embryo is then transferred to female tract. Choose the correct option:
questions.option_a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.option_b: Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
questions.option_c: A is true but R is false
questions.option_d: A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both true; R completes test-tube baby protocol.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Assertion (A): Infertility is failure to conceive after 2 years unprotected cohabitation. Reason (R): ART can assist such couples. Choose the correct option:
questions.option_a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.option_b: Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
questions.option_c: A is true but R is false
questions.option_d: A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both true but R is not explanation of definition—B correct AR option.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which is INCORRECT about MTP?
questions.option_c: Always preferred over contraception for routine birth control
questions.option_d: Misuse for sex selection is illegal
questions.explanation: Contraception preferred; MTP not routine birth control.
